name: connecticut
sentence: Its capital is Hartford, and its most populous city is Bridgeport.

name: connecticut
sentence: Historically, the state is part of New England as well as the tri-state area with New York and New Jersey.

name: connecticut
sentence: The state is named for the Connecticut River which approximately bisects the state.

name: connecticut
sentence: The word Connecticut is derived from various anglicized spellings of Quinnetuket, a Mohegan-Pequot word for "long tidal river".Connecticut's first European settlers were Dutchmen who established a small, short-lived settlement called House of Hope in Hartford at the confluence of the Park and Connecticut Rivers.

name: connecticut
sentence: Half of Connecticut was initially claimed by the Dutch colony New Netherland, which included much of the land between the Connecticut and Delaware Rivers, although the first major settlements were established in the 1630s by the English.

name: connecticut
sentence: Thomas Hooker led a band of followers from the Massachusetts Bay Colony and founded the Connecticut Colony; other settlers from Massachusetts founded the Saybrook Colony and the New Haven Colony.

name: connecticut
sentence: The Connecticut and New Haven colonies established documents of Fundamental Orders, considered the first constitutions in America.

name: connecticut
sentence: In 1662, the three colonies were merged under a royal charter, making Connecticut a crown colony.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut was one of the Thirteen Colonies which rejected British rule in the American Revolution.

name: connecticut
sentence: It was influential in the development of the federal government of the United States.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut is the third-smallest state by area, the 29th most populous, and the fourth most densely populated of the fifty states.

name: connecticut
sentence: It is known as the "Constitution State", the "Nutmeg State", the "Provisions State", and the "Land of Steady Habits".

name: connecticut
sentence: The Connecticut River, Thames River, and ports along Long Island Sound have given Connecticut a strong maritime tradition which continues today.

name: connecticut
sentence: The state also has a long history of hosting the financial services industry, including insurance companies in Hartford County and hedge funds in Fairfield County.

name: connecticut
sentence: As of the 2010 census, it has the highest per-capita income, second-highest level of human development behind Massachusetts, and highest median household income in the United States.

name: connecticut
sentence: The name Connecticut is derived from the Mohegan-Pequot word that has been translated as "long tidal river" and "upon the long river", both referring to the Connecticut River.

name: connecticut
sentence: Evidence of human presence in the Connecticut region dates to as much as 10,000 years ago.

name: connecticut
sentence: Stone tools were used for hunting, fishing, and woodworking.

name: connecticut
sentence: Semi-nomadic in lifestyle, these peoples moved seasonally to take advantage of various resources in the area.

name: connecticut
sentence: They shared languages based on Algonquian.

name: connecticut
sentence: The Connecticut region was inhabited by multiple Native American tribes which can be grouped into the Nipmuc, the Sequin or "River Indians" (which included the Tunxis, Schaghticoke, Podunk, Wangunk, Hammonasset, and Quinnipiac), the Mattabesec or "Wappinger Confederacy" and the Pequot-Mohegan.

name: connecticut
sentence: Some of these groups still reside in Connecticut, including the Mohegans, the Pequots, and the Paugusetts.

name: connecticut
sentence: The first European explorer in Connecticut was Dutchman Adriaen Block, who explored the region in 1614.

name: connecticut
sentence: Dutch fur traders then sailed up the Connecticut River, which they called Versche Rivier ("Fresh River"), and built a fort at Dutch Point in Hartford that they named "House of Hope" (Dutch: Huis van Hoop).The Connecticut Colony was originally a number of separate, smaller settlements at Windsor, Wethersfield, Saybrook, Hartford, and New Haven.

name: connecticut
sentence: The first English settlers came in 1633 and settled at Windsor, and then at Wethersfield the following year.

name: connecticut
sentence: John Winthrop the Younger of Massachusetts received a commission to create Saybrook Colony at the mouth of the Connecticut River in 1635.The main body of settlers came in one large group in 1636.

name: connecticut
sentence: They were Puritans from Massachusetts Bay Colony led by Thomas Hooker, who established the Connecticut Colony at Hartford.

name: connecticut
sentence: The Fundamental Orders of Connecticut were adopted in January 1639, and have been described as the first constitutional document in America.The Quinnipiack Colony was established by John Davenport, Theophilus Eaton, and others at New Haven in March 1638.

name: connecticut
sentence: The New Haven Colony had its own constitution called "The Fundamental Agreement of the New Haven Colony", signed on June 4, 1639.The settlements were established without official sanction of the English Crown, and each was an independent political entity.

name: connecticut
sentence: In 1662, Winthrop traveled to England and obtained a charter from Charles II which united the settlements of Connecticut.

name: connecticut
sentence: Historically important colonial settlements included Windsor (1633), Wethersfield (1634), Saybrook (1635), Hartford (1636), New Haven (1638), Fairfield (1639), Guilford (1639), Milford (1639), Stratford (1639), Farmington (1640), Stamford (1641), and New London (1646).

name: connecticut
sentence: The Pequot War marked the first major clash between colonists and Native Americans in New England.

name: connecticut
sentence: The Pequots reacted with increasing aggression to Colonial settlements in their territory—while simultaneously taking lands from the Narragansett and Mohegan tribes.

name: connecticut
sentence: Settlers responded to a murder in 1636 with a raid on a Pequot village on Block Island; the Pequots laid siege to Saybrook Colony's garrison that autumn, then raided Wethersfield in the spring of 1637.

name: connecticut
sentence: Colonists declared war on the Pequots, organized a band of militia and allies from the Mohegan and Narragansett tribes, and attacked a Pequot village on the Mystic River, with death toll estimates ranging between 300 and 700 Pequots.

name: connecticut
sentence: After suffering another major loss at a battle in Fairfield, the Pequots asked for a truce and peace terms.The western boundaries of Connecticut have been subject to change over time.

name: connecticut
sentence: The Hartford Treaty with the Dutch was signed on September 19, 1650, but it was never ratified by the British.

name: connecticut
sentence: According to it, the western boundary of Connecticut ran north from Greenwich Bay for a distance of 20 miles (32 km), "provided the said line come not within 10 miles of Hudson River".

name: connecticut
sentence: This agreement was observed by both sides until war erupted between England and The Netherlands in 1652.

name: connecticut
sentence: Conflict continued concerning colonial limits until the Duke of York captured New Netherland in 1664.On the other hand, Connecticut's original Charter in 1662 granted it all the land to the "South Sea"—that is, to the Pacific Ocean.

name: connecticut
sentence: Most Colonial royal grants were for long east–west strips.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut took its grant seriously and established a ninth county between the Susquehanna River and Delaware River named Westmoreland County.

name: connecticut
sentence: This resulted in the brief Pennamite Wars with Pennsylvania.Yale College was established in 1701, providing Connecticut with an important institution to educate clergy and civil leaders.

name: connecticut
sentence: The Congregational church dominated religious life in the colony and, by extension, town affairs in many parts.With more than 600 miles of coastline including along its navigable rivers, Connecticut developed during its colonial years the antecedents of a maritime tradition that would later produce booms in shipbuilding, marine transport, naval support, seafood production, and leisure boating.

name: connecticut
sentence: Historical records list the Tryall as the first vessel built in Connecticut Colony, in 1649 at a site on the Connecticut River in present-day Wethersfield.

name: connecticut
sentence: In the two decades leading up to 1776 and the American Revolution, Connecticut boatyards launched about 100 sloops, schooners and brigs according to a database of US customs records maintained online by the Mystic Seaport Museum, the largest being the 180-ton Patient Mary launched in New Haven in 1763.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut's first lighthouse was constructed in 1760 at the mouth of the Thames River with the New London Harbor Lighthouse.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut designated four delegates to the Second Continental Congress who signed the Declaration of Independence: Samuel Huntington, Roger Sherman, William Williams, and Oliver Wolcott.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut's legislature authorized the outfitting of six new regiments in 1775, in the wake of the clashes between British regulars and Massachusetts militia at Lexington and Concord.

name: connecticut
sentence: There were some 1,200 Connecticut troops on hand at the Battle of Bunker Hill in June 1775.

name: connecticut
sentence: In 1775, David Bushnell invented the Turtle which the following year launched the first submarine attack in history, unsuccessfully against a British warship at anchor in New York Harbor.In 1777, the British got word of Continental Army supplies in Danbury, and they landed an expeditionary force of some 2,000 troops in Westport.

name: connecticut
sentence: This force then marched to Danbury and destroyed homes and much of the depot.

name: connecticut
sentence: Continental Army troops and militia led by General David Wooster and General Benedict Arnold engaged them on their return march at Ridgefield in 1777.

name: connecticut
sentence: For the winter of 1778–79, General George Washington decided to split the Continental Army into three divisions encircling New York City, where British General Sir Henry Clinton had taken up winter quarters.

name: connecticut
sentence: Major General Israel Putnam chose Redding as the winter encampment quarters for some 3,000 regulars and militia under his command.

name: connecticut
sentence: The Redding encampment allowed Putnam's soldiers to guard the replenished supply depot in Danbury and to support any operations along Long Island Sound and the Hudson River Valley.

name: connecticut
sentence: Some of the men were veterans of the winter encampment at Valley Forge, Pennsylvania, the previous winter.

name: connecticut
sentence: Soldiers at the Redding camp endured supply shortages, cold temperatures, and significant snow, with some historians dubbing the encampment "Connecticut's Valley Forge".The state was also the launching site for a number of raids against Long Island orchestrated by Samuel Holden Parsons and Benjamin Tallmadge, and provided soldiers and material for the war effort, especially to Washington's army outside New York City.

name: connecticut
sentence: General William Tryon raided the Connecticut coast in July 1779, focusing on New Haven, Norwalk, and Fairfield.

name: connecticut
sentence: New London and Groton Heights were raided in September 1781 by Benedict Arnold, who had turned traitor to the British.At the outset of the American Revolution, the Continental Congress assigned Nathaniel Shaw Jr. of New London as its naval agent in charge of recruiting privateers to seize British vessels as opportunities presented, with nearly 50 operating out of the Thames River which eventually drew the reprisal from the British force led by Arnold.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut ratified the US Constitution on January 9, 1788, becoming the fifth state.The state prospered during the era following the American Revolution, as mills and textile factories were built and seaports flourished from trade and fisheries.

name: connecticut
sentence: After Congress established in 1790 the predecessor to the US Revenue Cutter Service that would evolve into the US Coast Guard, President Washington assigned Jonathan Maltbie as one of seven masters to enforce customs regulations, with Maltbie monitoring the southern New England coast with a 48-foot cutter sloop named Argus.In 1786, Connecticut ceded territory to the US government that became part of the Northwest Territory.

name: connecticut
sentence: The state retained land extending across the northern part of present-day Ohio called the Connecticut Western Reserve.

name: connecticut
sentence: The Western Reserve section was settled largely by people from Connecticut, and they brought Connecticut place names to Ohio.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut made agreements with Pennsylvania and New York which extinguished the land claims within those states' boundaries and created the Connecticut Panhandle.

name: connecticut
sentence: The state then ceded the Western Reserve in 1800 to the federal government, which brought it to its present boundaries (other than minor adjustments with Massachusetts).

name: connecticut
sentence: For the first time in 1800, Connecticut shipwrights launched more than 100 vessels in a single year.

name: connecticut
sentence: Over the following decade to the doorstep of renewed hostilities with Britain that sparked the War of 1812, Connecticut boatyards constructed close to 1,000 vessels, the most productive stretch of any decade in the 19th century.During the war, the British launched raids in Stonington and Essex and blockaded vessels in the Thames River.

name: connecticut
sentence: Derby native Isaac Hull became Connecticut's best-known naval figure to win renown during the conflict, as captain of the USConstitution.

name: connecticut
sentence: The British blockade during the War of 1812 hurt exports and bolstered the influence of Federalists who opposed the war.

name: connecticut
sentence: The cessation of imports from Britain stimulated the construction of factories to manufacture textiles and machinery.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut came to be recognized as a major center for manufacturing, due in part to the inventions of Eli Whitney and other early innovators of the Industrial Revolution.The war led to the development of fast clippers that helped extend the reach of New England merchants to the Pacific and Indian oceans.

name: connecticut
sentence: The first half of the 19th century saw as well a rapid rise in whaling, with New London emerging as one of the New England industry's three biggest home ports after Nantucket and New Bedford.The state was known for its political conservatism, typified by its Federalist party and the Yale College of Timothy Dwight.

name: connecticut
sentence: The foremost intellectuals were Dwight and Noah Webster, who compiled his great dictionary in New Haven.

name: connecticut
sentence: Religious tensions polarized the state, as the Congregational Church struggled to maintain traditional viewpoints, in alliance with the Federalists.

name: connecticut
sentence: The failure of the Hartford Convention in 1814 hurt the Federalist cause, with the Democratic-Republican Party gaining control in 1817.Connecticut had been governed under the "Fundamental Orders" since 1639, but the state adopted a new constitution in 1818.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut manufacturers played a major role in supplying the Union forces with weapons and supplies during the Civil War.

name: connecticut
sentence: The state furnished 55,000 men, formed into thirty full regiments of infantry, including two in the US

name: connecticut
sentence: Colored Troops, with several Connecticut men becoming generals.

name: connecticut
sentence: The Navy attracted 250 officers and 2,100 men, and Glastonbury native Gideon Welles was Secretary of the Navy.

name: connecticut
sentence: James H. Ward of Hartford was the first US

name: connecticut
sentence: Naval Officer killed in the Civil War.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut casualties included 2,088 killed in combat, 2,801 dying from disease, and 689 dying in Confederate prison camps.A surge of national unity in 1861 brought thousands flocking to the colors from every town and city.

name: connecticut
sentence: However, as the war became a crusade to end slavery, many Democrats (especially Irish Catholics) pulled back.

name: connecticut
sentence: The Democrats took a pro-slavery position and included many Copperheads willing to let the South secede.

name: connecticut
sentence: The intensely fought 1863 election for governor was narrowly won by the Republicans.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut's extensive industry, dense population, flat terrain, and wealth encouraged the construction of railroads starting in 1839.

name: connecticut
sentence: By 1840, 102 miles (164 km) of line were in operation, growing to 402 miles (647 km) in 1850 and 601 miles (967 km) in 1860.The New York, New Haven and Hartford Railroad, called the New Haven or "The Consolidated", became the dominant Connecticut railroad company after 1872.

name: connecticut
sentence: J. P. Morgan began financing the major New England railroads in the 1890s, dividing territory so that they would not compete.

name: connecticut
sentence: The New Haven purchased 50 smaller companies, including steamship lines, and built a network of light rails (electrified trolleys) that provided inter-urban transportation for all of southern New England.

name: connecticut
sentence: By 1912, the New Haven operated over 2,000 miles (3,200 km) of track with 120,000 employees.As steam-powered passenger ships proliferated after the Civil War, Noank would produce the two largest built in Connecticut during the 19th century, with the 332-foot wooden steam paddle wheeler Rhode Island launched in 1882, and the 345-foot paddle wheeler Connecticut seven years later.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut shipyards would launch more than 165 steam-powered vessels in the 19th century.In 1875, the first telephone exchange in the world was established in New Haven.

name: connecticut
sentence: When World War I broke out in 1914, Connecticut became a major supplier of weaponry to the US military; by 1918, 80% of the state's industries were producing goods for the war effort.

name: connecticut
sentence: Remington Arms in Bridgeport produced half the small-arms cartridges used by the US Army, with other major suppliers including Winchester in New Haven and Colt in Hartford.Connecticut was also an important US Navy supplier, with Electric Boat receiving orders for 85 submarines, Lake Torpedo Boat building more than 20 subs, and the Groton Iron Works building freighters.

name: connecticut
sentence: On June 21, 1916, the Navy made Groton the site for its East Coast submarine base and school.

name: connecticut
sentence: The state enthusiastically supported the American war effort in 1917 and 1918 with large purchases of war bonds, a further expansion of industry, and an emphasis on increasing food production on the farms.

name: connecticut
sentence: Thousands of state, local, and volunteer groups mobilized for the war effort and were coordinated by the Connecticut State Council of Defense.

name: connecticut
sentence: Manufacturers wrestled with manpower shortages; Waterbury's American Brass and Manufacturing Company was running at half capacity, so the federal government agreed to furlough soldiers to work there.

name: connecticut
sentence: In 1919, J. Henry Roraback started the Connecticut Light & Power Co. which became the state's dominant electric utility.

name: connecticut
sentence: In 1925, Frederick Rentschler spurred the creation of Pratt & Whitney in Hartford to develop engines for aircraft; the company became an important military supplier in World War II and one of the three major manufacturers of jet engines in the world.On September 21, 1938, the most destructive storm in New England history struck eastern Connecticut, killing hundreds of people.

name: connecticut
sentence: The eye of the "Long Island Express" passed just west of New Haven and devastated the Connecticut shoreline between Old Saybrook and Stonington from the full force of wind and waves, even though they had partial protection by Long Island.

name: connecticut
sentence: The hurricane caused extensive damage to infrastructure, homes, and businesses.

name: connecticut
sentence: In New London, a 500-foot (150 m) sailing ship was driven into a warehouse complex, causing a major fire.

name: connecticut
sentence: Heavy rainfall caused the Connecticut River to flood downtown Hartford and East Hartford.

name: connecticut
sentence: An estimated 50,000 trees fell onto roadways.

name: connecticut
sentence: The advent of lend-lease in support of Britain helped lift Connecticut from the Great Depression, with the state a major production center for weaponry and supplies used in World War II.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut manufactured 4.1% of total US military armaments produced during the war, ranking ninth among the 48 states, with major factories including Colt for firearms, Pratt & Whitney for aircraft engines, Chance Vought for fighter planes, Hamilton Standard for propellers, and Electric Boat for submarines and PT boats.

name: connecticut
sentence: In Bridgeport, General Electric produced a significant new weapon to combat tanks: the bazooka.On May 13, 1940, Igor Sikorsky made an untethered flight of the first practical helicopter.

name: connecticut
sentence: The helicopter saw limited use in World War II, but future military production made Sikorsky Aircraft's Stratford plant Connecticut's largest single manufacturing site by the start of the 21st century.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut lost some wartime factories following the end of hostilities, but the state shared in a general post-war expansion that included the construction of highways and resulting in middle-class growth in suburban areas.

name: connecticut
sentence: Prescott Bush represented Connecticut in the US Senatorte from 1952 to 1963; his son George H W Bush and grandson George W. Bush both became presidents of the United States.

name: connecticut
sentence: In 1965, Connecticut ratified its current constitution, replacing the document that had served since 1818.In 1968, commercial operation began for the Connecticut Yankee Nuclear Power Plant in Haddam; in 1970, the Millstone Nuclear Power Station began operations in Waterford.

name: connecticut
sentence: In 1974, Connecticut elected Democratic Governor Ella T. Grasso, who became the first woman in any state to be elected governor without being the wife or widow of a previous governor.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut's dependence on the defense industry posed an economic challenge at the end of the Cold War.

name: connecticut
sentence: The resulting budget crisis helped elect Lowell Weicker as governor on a third-party ticket in 1990.

name: connecticut
sentence: Weicker's remedy was a state income tax which proved effective in balancing the budget, but only for the short-term.

name: connecticut
sentence: He did not run for a second term, in part because of this politically unpopular move.In 1992, initial construction was completed on Foxwoods Casino at the Mashantucket Pequots reservation in eastern Connecticut, which became the largest casino in the Western Hemisphere.

name: connecticut
sentence: Mohegan Sun followed four years later.

name: connecticut
sentence: In 2000, presidential candidate Al Gore chose Senatortor Joe Lieberman as his running mate, marking the first time that a major party presidential ticket included someone of the Jewish faith.

name: connecticut
sentence: Gore and Lieberman fell five votes short of George W. Bush and Dick Cheney in the Electoral College.

name: connecticut
sentence: In the terrorist attacks of September 11, 2001, 65 state residents were killed, mostly Fairfield County residents who were working in the World Trade Center.

name: connecticut
sentence: In 2004, Republican Governor John G. Rowland resigned during a corruption investigation, later pleading guilty to federal charges.Connecticut was hit by three major storms in just over 14 months in 2011 and 2012, with all three causing extensive property damage and electric outages.

name: connecticut
sentence: Hurricane Irene struck Connecticut August 28, and damage totaled $235 million.

name: connecticut
sentence: Two months later, the "Halloween nor'easter" dropped extensive snow onto trees, resulting in snapped branches and trunks that damaged power lines; some areas were without electricity for 11 days.

name: connecticut
sentence: Hurricane Sandy had tropical storm-force winds when it reached Connecticut October 29, 2012.

name: connecticut
sentence: Sandy's winds drove storm surges into streets and cut power to 98% of homes and businesses, with more than $360 million in damage.On December 14, 2012, Adam Lanza shot and killed 26 people at Sandy Hook Elementary School in Newtown, and then killed himself.

name: connecticut
sentence: The massacre spurred renewed efforts by activists for tighter laws on gun ownership nationally.In the summer and fall of 2016, Connecticut experienced a drought in many parts of the state, causing some water-use bans.

name: connecticut
sentence: As of November 15, 2016 (2016-11-15), 45% of the state was listed at Severe Drought by the US Drought Monitor, including almost all of Hartford and Litchfield counties.

name: connecticut
sentence: All the rest of the state was in Moderate Drought or Severe Drought, including Middlesex, Fairfield, New London, New Haven, Windham, and Tolland counties.

name: connecticut
sentence: This affected the agricultural economy in the state.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut is bordered on the south by Long Island Sound, on the west by New York, on the north by Massachusetts, and on the east by Rhode Island.

name: connecticut
sentence: The state capital and fourth largest city is Hartford, and other major cities and towns (by population) include Bridgeport, New Haven, Stamford, Waterbury, Norwalk, Danbury, New Britain, Greenwich, and Bristol.

name: connecticut
sentence: There are 169 incorporated towns in Connecticut, with cities and villages included within some towns.

name: connecticut
sentence: The highest peak in Connecticut is Bear Mountain in Salisbury in the northwest corner of the state.

name: connecticut
sentence: The highest point is just east of where Connecticut, Massachusetts, and New York meet (42°3′ N, 73°29′ W), on the southern slope of Mount Frissell, whose peak lies nearby in Massachusetts.

name: connecticut
sentence: At the opposite extreme, many of the coastal towns have areas that are less than 20 feet (6.1 m) above sea level.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut has a long maritime history and a reputation based on that history—yet the state has no direct oceanfront (technically speaking).

name: connecticut
sentence: The coast of Connecticut sits on Long Island Sound, which is an estuary.

name: connecticut
sentence: The state's access to the open Atlantic Ocean is both to the west (toward New York City) and to the east (toward the "race" near Rhode Island).

name: connecticut
sentence: Due to this unique geography, Long Island Sound and the Connecticut shoreline are relatively protected from high waves from storms.The Connecticut River cuts through the center of the state, flowing into Long Island Sound.

name: connecticut
sentence: The most populous metropolitan region centered within the state lies in the Connecticut River Valley.

name: connecticut
sentence: Despite Connecticut's relatively small size, it features wide regional variations in its landscape; for example, in the northwestern Litchfield Hills, it features rolling mountains and horse farms, whereas in areas to the east of New Haven along the coast, the landscape features coastal marshes, beaches, and large scale maritime activities.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut's rural areas and small towns in the northeast and northwest corners of the state contrast sharply with its industrial cities such as Stamford, Bridgeport, and New Haven, located along the coastal highways from the New York border to New London, then northward up the Connecticut River to Hartford.

name: connecticut
sentence: Many towns in northeastern and northwestern Connecticut center around a green.

name: connecticut
sentence: Near the green typically stand historical visual symbols of New England towns, such as a white church, a colonial meeting house, a colonial tavern or inn, several colonial houses, and so on, establishing a scenic historical appearance maintained for both historic preservation and tourism.

name: connecticut
sentence: Many of the areas in southern and coastal Connecticut have been built up and rebuilt over the years, and look less visually like traditional New England.

name: connecticut
sentence: The northern boundary of the state with Massachusetts is marked by the Southwick Jog or Granby Notch, an approximately 2.5 miles (4.0 km) square detour into Connecticut.

name: connecticut
sentence: The origin of this anomaly is clearly established in a long line of disputes and temporary agreements which were finally concluded in 1804, when southern Southwick's residents sought to leave Massachusetts, and the town was split in half.The southwestern border of Connecticut where it abuts New York State is marked by a panhandle in Fairfield County, containing the towns of Greenwich, Stamford, New Canaan, Darien, and parts of Norwalk and Wilton.

name: connecticut
sentence: This irregularity in the boundary is the result of territorial disputes in the late 17th century, culminating with New York giving up its claim to the area, whose residents considered themselves part of Connecticut, in exchange for an equivalent area extending northwards from Ridgefield to the Massachusetts border, as well as undisputed claim to Rye, New York.Areas maintained by the National Park Service include Appalachian National Scenic Trail, Quinebaug and Shetucket Rivers Valley National Heritage Corridor, and Weir Farm National Historic Site.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut lies at the rough transition zone between the southern end of the humid continental climate, and the northern portion of the humid subtropical climate.

name: connecticut
sentence: Northern Connecticut generally experiences a climate with cold winters with moderate snowfall and hot, humid summers.

name: connecticut
sentence: Far southern and coastal Connecticut has a climate with cool winters with a mix of rain and infrequent snow, and the long hot and humid summers typical of the middle and lower East Coast.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut sees a fairly even precipitation pattern with rainfall/snowfall spread throughout the 12 months.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut averages 56% of possible sunshine (higher than the US national average), averaging 2,400 hours of sunshine annually.

name: connecticut
sentence: On average, about one third of days in the state see some amount of precipitation each year.

name: connecticut
sentence: Occasionally, some months may see extremes in precipitation, either much higher or lower than normal, though long term droughts and floods are rare.Early spring can range from slightly cool (40s to low 50s F) to warm (65 to 70 F), while mid and late spring (late April/May) is warm.

name: connecticut
sentence: By late May, the building Bermuda High creates a southerly flow of warm and humid tropical air, bringing hot weather conditions throughout the state.

name: connecticut
sentence: Average highs are 81 °F (27 °C) in New London and 85 °F (29 °C) in Windsor Locks at the peak of summer in late July.

name: connecticut
sentence: On occasion, heat waves with highs from 90 to 100 °F (38 °C) occur across Connecticut.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut's record high temperature is 106 °F (41 °C) which occurred in Danbury on July 15, 1995.

name: connecticut
sentence: Although summers are sunny in Connecticut, quick moving summer thunderstorms can bring brief downpours with thunder and lightning.

name: connecticut
sentence: Occasionally these thunderstorms can be severe, and the state usually averages one tornado per year.

name: connecticut
sentence: During hurricane season, the remains of tropical cyclones occasionally affect the region, though a direct hit is rare.

name: connecticut
sentence: Some notable hurricanes to impact the state include the 1938 New England hurricane, Hurricane Carol in 1954, Hurricane Sandy in 2012, and Hurricane Isaias in 2020.Weather commonly associated with the fall season typically begins in October and lasts to the first days of December.

name: connecticut
sentence: Daily high temperatures in October and November range from the 50s to 60s (Fahrenheit) with nights in the 40s and upper 30s.

name: connecticut
sentence: Colorful foliage begins across northern parts of the state in early October and moves south and east reaching southeast Connecticut by early November.

name: connecticut
sentence: Far southern and coastal areas, however, have more oak and hickory trees (and fewer maples) and are often less colorful than areas to the north.

name: connecticut
sentence: By December daytime highs are in the 40s °F for much of the state, and average overnight lows are below freezing.

name: connecticut
sentence: Winters (December through mid-March) are generally cold from south to north in Connecticut.

name: connecticut
sentence: The coldest month (January) has average high temperatures ranging from 38 °F (3 °C) in the coastal lowlands to 33 °F (1 °C) in the inland and northern portions on the state.

name: connecticut
sentence: The lowest temperature recorded in Connecticut is −32 °F (−36 °C) which has been observed twice: in Falls Village on February 16, 1943, and in Coventry on January 22, 1961.

name: connecticut
sentence: The average yearly snowfall ranges from about 60 inches (1,500 mm) in the higher elevations of the northern portion of the state to only 20–25 inches (510–640 mm) along the southeast coast of Connecticut (Branford to Groton).

name: connecticut
sentence: Generally, any locale north or west of Interstate 84 receives the most snow, during a storm, and throughout the season.

name: connecticut
sentence: Most of Connecticut has less than 60 days of snow cover.

name: connecticut
sentence: Snow usually falls from late November to late March in the northern part of the state, and from early December to mid-March in the southern and coastal parts of the state.

name: connecticut
sentence: During winter every few years, Connecticut can occasionally get heavy snowstorms, called nor'easters, which may produce as much as two feet of snow on rare occasions.

name: connecticut
sentence: Ice storms also occur on occasion, such as the Southern New England ice storm of 1973 and the December 2008 Northeastern United States ice storm.

name: connecticut
sentence: These storms can cause widespread power outages and damage.

name: connecticut
sentence: Forests consist of a mix of Northeastern coastal forests of oak in southern areas of the state, to the upland New England-Acadian forests in the northwestern parts of the state.

name: connecticut
sentence: Mountain Laurel (Kalmia latifolia) is the state flower and is native to low ridges in several parts of Connecticut.

name: connecticut
sentence: Rosebay rhododendron (Rhododendron maximum) is also native to eastern uplands of Connecticut and Pachaug State Forest is home to the Rhododendron Sanctuary Trail.

name: connecticut
sentence: Atlantic white cedar (Chamaecyparis thyoides), is found in wetlands in the southern parts of the state.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut has one native cactus (Opuntia humifusa), found in sandy coastal areas and low hillsides.

name: connecticut
sentence: Several types of beach grasses and wildflowers are also native to Connecticut.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut spans USDA Plant Hardiness Zones 5b to 7a.

name: connecticut
sentence: Coastal Connecticut is the broad transition zone where more southern and subtropical plants are cultivated.

name: connecticut
sentence: In some coastal communities, Magnolia grandiflora (southern magnolia), crape myrtles, scrub palms (Sabal minor), needle palms (Rhapidophyllum hystrix), and other broadleaved evergreens are cultivated in small numbers.

name: connecticut
sentence: As of the 2020 United States census, Connecticut has a population of 3,605,944, an increase of 31,847 people (0.9%) from the 2010 United States census.

name: connecticut
sentence: Among the census records, 20.4% of the population was under 18.

name: connecticut
sentence: In 1790, 97% of the population in Connecticut was classified as "rural".

name: connecticut
sentence: The first census in which less than half the population was classified as rural was 1890.

name: connecticut
sentence: In the 2000 census, only 12.3% was considered rural.

name: connecticut
sentence: Most of western and southern Connecticut (particularly the Gold Coast) is strongly associated with New York City; this area is the most affluent and populous region of the state and has high property costs and high incomes.

name: connecticut
sentence: The center of population of Connecticut is located in the town of Cheshire.According to HUD's 2022 Annual Homeless Assessment Report, there were an estimated 2,930 homeless people in Connecticut.

name: connecticut
sentence: In common with the majority of the United States, non-Hispanic whites have remained the dominant racial and ethnic group in Connecticut.

name: connecticut
sentence: From being 98% of the population in 1940, however, they have declined to 63% of the population as of the 2020 census.

name: connecticut
sentence: These statistics have represented fewer Americans identifying as non-Hispanic white, which has given rise to the Hispanic and Latino American population and Asian American population overall.

name: connecticut
sentence: As of 2011, 46.1% of Connecticut's population younger than age 1 were minorities.

name: connecticut
sentence: As of 2004, 11.4% of the population (400,000) was foreign-born.

name: connecticut
sentence: In 1870, native-born Americans had accounted for 75% of the state's population, but that had dropped to 35% by 1918.

name: connecticut
sentence: Also as of 2000, 81.69% of Connecticut residents age 5 and older spoke English at home and 8.42% spoke Spanish, followed by Italian at 1.59%, French at 1.31%, and Polish at 1.20%.The largest ancestry groups since 2010 were: 19.3% Italian, 17.9% Irish, 10.7% English, 10.4% German, 8.6% Polish, 6.6% French, 3.0% French Canadian, 2.7% American, 2.0% Scottish, and 1.4% Scotch Irish.

name: connecticut
sentence: Note: Births in table do not add up because Hispanics are counted both by their ethnicity and by their race, giving a higher overall number.

name: connecticut
sentence: Since 2016, data for births of White Hispanic origin are not collected, but included in one Hispanic group; persons of Hispanic origin may be of any race.

name: connecticut
sentence: A Pew survey of Connecticut residents' religious self-identification showed the following distribution of affiliations in 2014: Protestant 35%, Mormonism 1%, Jewish 3%, Roman Catholic 33%, Orthodox 1%, Non-religious 28%, Jehovah's Witness 1%, Hinduism 1%, Buddhism 1% and Islam 1%.

name: connecticut
sentence: Jewish congregations had 108,280 (3.2%) members in 2000.The Jewish population is concentrated in the towns near Long Island Sound between Greenwich and New Haven, in Greater New Haven and in Greater Hartford, especially the suburb of West Hartford.

name: connecticut
sentence: According to the Association of Religion Data Archives, the largest Christian denominations, by number of adherents, in 2010 were: the Catholic Church, with 1,252,936; the United Church of Christ, with 96,506; and non-denominational Evangelical Protestants, with 72,863.Recent immigration has brought other non-Christian religions to the state, but the numbers of adherents of other religions are still low.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut is also home to New England's largest Protestant church: The First Cathedral in Bloomfield, Connecticut, located in Hartford County.

name: connecticut
sentence: Hartford is seat to the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Hartford, which is sovereign over the Diocese of Bridgeport and the Diocese of Norwich.

name: connecticut
sentence: By the Public Religion Research Institute's study in 2020, 71% of the population identified as Christian.

name: connecticut
sentence: In contrast to the 2014 study by the Pew Research Center, the irreligious declined from 28% of the population to 21% at the 2020 Public Religion Research Institute's study.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut's economic output in 2019 as measured by gross domestic product was $289 billion, up from $277.9 billion in 2018.Connecticut's per capita personal income in 2019 was estimated at $79,087, the highest of any state.

name: connecticut
sentence: There is, however, a great disparity in incomes throughout the state; after New York, Connecticut had the second largest gap nationwide between the average incomes of the top 1% and the average incomes of the bottom 99%.

name: connecticut
sentence: According to a 2018 study by Phoenix Marketing International, Connecticut had the third-largest number of millionaires per capita in the United States, with a ratio of 7.75%.

name: connecticut
sentence: New Canaan is the wealthiest town in Connecticut, with a per capita income of $85,459.

name: connecticut
sentence: Hartford is the poorest municipality in Connecticut, with a per capita income of $13,428 in 2000.As of December 2019, Connecticut's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate was 3.8%, with US unemployment at 3.5% that month.

name: connecticut
sentence: Dating back to 1982, Connecticut recorded its lowest unemployment in 2000 between August and October, at 2.2%.

name: connecticut
sentence: The highest unemployment rate during that period occurred in November and December 2010 at 9.3%, but economists expect record new levels of layoffs as a result of business closures in the spring of 2020 as the result of the coronavirus pandemic.

name: connecticut
sentence: Tax is collected by the Connecticut Department of Revenue Services and by local municipalities.As of 2012, Connecticut residents had the second highest rate in the nation of combined state and local taxes after New York, at 12.6% of income compared to the national average of 9.9% as reported by the Tax Foundation.Before 1991, Connecticut had an investment-only income tax system.

name: connecticut
sentence: Income from employment was untaxed, but income from investments was taxed at 13%, the highest rate in the US, with no deductions allowed for costs of producing the investment income, such as interest on borrowing.

name: connecticut
sentence: In 1991, under Governor Lowell P. Weicker Jr., an independent, the system was changed to one in which the taxes on employment income and investment income were equalized at a maximum rate of 4%.

name: connecticut
sentence: The new tax policy drew investment firms to Connecticut; as of 2019, Fairfield County was home to the headquarters for 16 of the 200 largest hedge funds in the world.As of 2019, the income tax rates on Connecticut individuals were divided into seven tax brackets of 3% (on income up to $10,000); 5% ($10,000–$50,000); 5.5% ($50,000–$100,000); 6% ($100,000–$200,000); 6.5% ($200,000–$250,000); 6.9% ($250,000–$500,000); and 6.99% above $500,000, with additional amounts owed depending on the bracket.All wages of Connecticut residents are subject to the state's income tax, even if earned outside the state.

name: connecticut
sentence: However, in those cases, Connecticut income tax must be withheld only to the extent the Connecticut tax exceeds the amount withheld by the other jurisdiction.

name: connecticut
sentence: Since New York has higher income tax rates than Connecticut, this effectively means that Connecticut residents who work in New York have no Connecticut income tax withheld.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut permits a credit for taxes paid to other jurisdictions, but since residents who work in other states are still subject to Connecticut income taxation, they may owe taxes if the jurisdictional credit does not fully offset the Connecticut tax amount.Connecticut levies a 6.35% state sales tax on the retail sale, lease, or rental of most goods.

name: connecticut
sentence: Some items and services in general are not subject to sales and use taxes unless specifically enumerated as taxable by statute.

name: connecticut
sentence: A provision excluding clothing under $50 from sales tax was repealed as of July 1, 2011.

name: connecticut
sentence: There are no additional sales taxes imposed by local jurisdictions.

name: connecticut
sentence: In 2001, Connecticut instituted what became an annual sales tax "holiday" each August lasting one week, when retailers do not have to remit sales tax on certain items and quantities of clothing that has varied from year to year.State law authorizes municipalities to tax property, including real estate, vehicles and other personal property, with state statute providing varying exemptions, credits and abatements.

name: connecticut
sentence: All assessments are at 70% of fair market value.

name: connecticut
sentence: The maximum property tax credit is $200 per return and any excess may not be refunded or carried forward.

name: connecticut
sentence: According to the Tax Foundation, on a per capita basis in the 2017 fiscal year Connecticut residents paid the 3rd highest average property taxes in the nation after New Hampshire and New Jersey.As of January 1, 2020, gasoline taxes and fees in Connecticut were 40.13 cents per gallon, 11th highest in the United States which had a nationwide average of 36.13 cents a gallon excluding federal taxes.

name: connecticut
sentence: Diesel taxes and fees as of January 2020 in Connecticut were 46.50 cents per gallon, ninth highest nationally with the US average at 37.91 cents.

name: connecticut
sentence: In 2019, sales of single-family homes in Connecticut totaled 33,146 units, a 2.1 percent decline from the 2018 transaction total.

name: connecticut
sentence: The median home sold in 2019 recorded a transaction amount of $260,000, up 0.4 percent from 2018.Connecticut had the seventh highest rate of home foreclosure activity in the country in 2019 at 0.53 percent of the total housing stock.

name: connecticut
sentence: Finance, insurance and real estate was Connecticut's largest industry in 2018 as ranked by gross domestic product, generating $75.7 billion in GDP that year.

name: connecticut
sentence: Major employers include The Hartford, Travelers, Harman International, Cigna, the Aetna subsidiary of CVS Health, Mass Mutual, People's United Financial, Bank of America, Realogy, Bridgewater Associates, GE Capital, William Raveis Real Estate, and Berkshire Hathaway through reinsurance and residential real estate subsidiaries.

name: connecticut
sentence: The combined educational, health and social services sector was the largest single industry as ranked by employment, with a combined workforce of 342,600 people at the end of 2019, ranking fourth the year before in GDP at $28.3 billion.

name: connecticut
sentence: The broad business and professional services sector had the second highest GDP total in Connecticut in 2018 at an estimated $33.7 billion.Manufacturing was the third biggest industry in 2018 with GDP of $30.8 billion, dominated by Raytheon Technologies formed in the March 2020 merger of Hartford-based United Technologies and Waltham, Mass.-based Raytheon Co. As of the merger, Raytheon Technologies employed about 19,000 people in Connecticut through subsidiaries Pratt & Whitney and Collins Aerospace.

name: connecticut
sentence: Lockheed Martin subsidiary Sikorsky Aircraft operates Connecticut's single largest manufacturing plant in Stratford, where it makes helicopters.

name: connecticut
sentence: The world's largest audio equipment manufacturing company Harman International is headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut.

name: connecticut
sentence: It owns many brands like JBL, Akg and Harman kardon.Other major manufacturers include the Electric Boat division of General Dynamics, which makes submarines in Groton, Boehringer Ingelheim, a pharmaceuticals manufacturer with its US headquarters in Ridgefield, and ASML, which in Wilton makes precision lithography machines used to create circuitry on semiconductors and flat-screen displays.Connecticut historically was a center of gun manufacturing, and four gun-manufacturing firms continued to operate in the state as of December 2012, employing 2,000 people: Colt, Stag, Ruger, and Mossberg.

name: connecticut
sentence: Marlin, owned by Remington, closed in April 2011.Other large components of the Connecticut economy in 2018 included wholesale trade ($18.1 billion in GDP); information services ($13.8 billion); retail ($13.7 billion); arts, entertainment and food services ($9.1 billion); and construction ($8.3 billion).Tourists spent $9.3 billion in Connecticut in 2017 according to estimates as part of a series of studies commissioned by the state of Connecticut.

name: connecticut
sentence: Foxwoods Resort Casino and Mohegan Sun are the two biggest tourist draws and number among the state's largest employers; both are located on Native American reservations in the southeastern Connecticut.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut's agricultural production totaled $580 million in 2017, with just over half of that revenue the result of nursery stock production.

name: connecticut
sentence: Milk production totaled $81 million that year, with other major product categories including eggs, vegetables and fruit, tobacco and shellfish.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut's economy uses less energy to produce each dollar of GDP than all other states except California, Massachusetts, and New York.

name: connecticut
sentence: It uses less energy on a per-capita basis than all but six other states.

name: connecticut
sentence: It has no fossil-fuel resources, but does have renewable resources.

name: connecticut
sentence: Average retail electricity prices are the highest among the 48 contiguous states.

name: connecticut
sentence: While the vast majority of state's overall energy consumption is fossil fuels, nuclear power delivered over 40% of state's electricity generation in 2019.

name: connecticut
sentence: Refuse-derived fuels and other biomass provided the largest share of renewable electricity at about a 3% share.

name: connecticut
sentence: Solar and wind generation have grown in recent years.

name: connecticut
sentence: More than three-quarters of solar generation came from distributed small-scale installations such as rooftop solar in 2019, and there is planning underway to significantly increase renewable generation with the state's offshore wind resource.

name: connecticut
sentence: The Interstate highways in the state are Interstate 95 (I-95) traveling southwest to northeast along the coast, I-84 traveling southwest to northeast in the center of the state, I-91 traveling north to south in the center of the state, and I-395 traveling north to south near the eastern border of the state.

name: connecticut
sentence: The other major highways in Connecticut are the Merritt Parkway and Wilbur Cross Parkway, which together form Connecticut Route 15 (Route 15), traveling from the Hutchinson River Parkway in New York parallel to I-95 before turning north of New Haven and traveling parallel to I-91, finally becoming a surface road in Berlin.

name: connecticut
sentence: I-95 and Route 15 were originally toll roads; they relied on a system of toll plazas at which all traffic stopped and paid fixed tolls.

name: connecticut
sentence: A series of major crashes at these plazas eventually contributed to the decision to remove the tolls in 1988.

name: connecticut
sentence: Other major arteries in the state include US Route 7 (US 7) in the west traveling parallel to the New York state line, Route 8 farther east near the industrial city of Waterbury and traveling north–south along the Naugatuck River Valley nearly parallel with US 7, and Route 9 in the east.

name: connecticut
sentence: Between New Haven and New York City, I-95 is one of the most congested highways in the United States.

name: connecticut
sentence: Although I-95 has been widened in several spots, some areas are only three lanes and this strains traffic capacity, resulting in frequent and lengthy rush hour delays.

name: connecticut
sentence: Frequently, the congestion spills over to clog the parallel Merritt Parkway and even US 1.

name: connecticut
sentence: The state has encouraged traffic reduction schemes, including rail use and ride-sharing.Connecticut also has a very active bicycling community, with one of the highest rates of bicycle ownership and use in the United States, particularly in New Haven.

name: connecticut
sentence: According to the US Census 2006 American Community Survey, New Haven has the highest percentage of commuters who bicycle to work of any major metropolitan center on the East Coast.

name: connecticut
sentence: Rail is a popular travel mode between New Haven and New York City's Grand Central Terminal.

name: connecticut
sentence: Southwestern Connecticut is served by the Metro-North Railroad's New Haven Line, operated by the Metropolitan Transportation Authority.

name: connecticut
sentence: Metro-North provides commuter service between New York City and New Haven, with branches to New Canaan, Danbury, and Waterbury.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut lies along Amtrak's Northeast Corridor, which features frequent Northeast Regional and Acela Express service from New Haven south to New York City, Philadelphia, Baltimore, Washington, DC, and Norfolk, VA, as well as north to New London, Providence and Boston.

name: connecticut
sentence: Since 1990, coastal cities and towns between New Haven and New London are also served by the Shore Line East commuter line.In June 2018, a commuter rail service called the Hartford Line began operating between New Haven and Springfield on Amtrak's New Haven-Springfield Line.

name: connecticut
sentence: Hartford Line service is provided by both Amtrak and the Connecticut Department of Transportation's CT Rail, and in addition to its termini serves New Haven State Street, Wallingford, Meriden, Berlin, Hartford, Windsor, and Windsor Locks.

name: connecticut
sentence: Several infill stations are planned to be added in the near future as of 2021.

name: connecticut
sentence: Amtrak's Vermonter runs from Washington to St. Albans, Vermont via the same line.

name: connecticut
sentence: In July 2019, Amtrak launched the Valley Flyer, which runs between New Haven and Greenfield, Massachusetts.A proposed commuter rail service, the Central Corridor Rail Line, would connect New London with Norwich, Willimantic, Storrs, and Stafford Springs, with service continuing into Massachusetts and Brattleboro, Vermont.

name: connecticut
sentence: Statewide bus service is supplied by Connecticut Transit, owned by the Connecticut Department of Transportation, with smaller municipal authorities providing local service.

name: connecticut
sentence: Bus networks are an important part of the transportation system in Connecticut, especially in urban areas like Hartford, Stamford, Norwalk, Bridgeport and New Haven.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut Transit also operates CTfastrak, a bus rapid transit service between New Britain and Hartford, which opened to the public on March 28, 2015.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut's largest airport is Bradley International Airport in Windsor Locks, 15 miles (24 km) north of Hartford.

name: connecticut
sentence: Many residents of central and southern Connecticut also make heavy use of JFK International Airport and Newark International Airports, especially for international travel.

name: connecticut
sentence: Smaller regional air service is provided at Tweed New Haven Regional Airport.

name: connecticut
sentence: Larger civil airports include Danbury Municipal Airport and Waterbury-Oxford Airport in western Connecticut, Hartford–Brainard Airport in central Connecticut, and Groton-New London Airport in eastern Connecticut.

name: connecticut
sentence: Sikorsky Memorial Airport is located in Stratford and mostly services cargo, helicopter and private aviation.

name: connecticut
sentence: Several ferry services cross Long Island Sound and connect the state to Long Island.

name: connecticut
sentence: The Bridgeport & Port Jefferson Ferry travels between Bridgeport, Connecticut, and Port Jefferson, New York.

name: connecticut
sentence: Ferry service also operates out of New London to Orient, New York; Fishers Island, New York; and Block Island, Rhode Island, which are popular tourist destinations.

name: connecticut
sentence: Two ferries cross the Connecticut River: the Rocky Hill–Glastonbury ferry and the Chester–Hadlyme ferry, the former of which is the oldest continuously operating ferry in the United States, operating since 1655.

name: connecticut
sentence: Hartford has been the sole capital of Connecticut since 1875.

name: connecticut
sentence: Before then, New Haven and Hartford alternated as dual capitals.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut is known as the "Constitution State".

name: connecticut
sentence: The origin of this nickname is uncertain, but it likely comes from Connecticut's pivotal role in the federal constitutional convention of 1787, during which Roger Sherman and Oliver Ellsworth helped to orchestrate what became known as the Connecticut Compromise, or the Great Compromise.

name: connecticut
sentence: This plan combined the Virginia Plan and the New Jersey Plan to form a bicameral legislature, a form copied by almost every state constitution since the adoption of the federal constitution.

name: connecticut
sentence: Variations of the bicameral legislature had been proposed by Virginia and New Jersey, but Connecticut's plan was the one that was in effect until the early 20th century, when Senatortors ceased to be selected by their state legislatures and were instead directly elected.

name: connecticut
sentence: Otherwise, it is still the design of Congress.

name: connecticut
sentence: The nickname also might refer to the Fundamental Orders of 1638–39.

name: connecticut
sentence: These Fundamental Orders represent the framework for the first formal Connecticut state government written by a representative body in Connecticut.

name: connecticut
sentence: The State of Connecticut government has operated under the direction of four separate documents in the course of the state's constitutional history.

name: connecticut
sentence: After the Fundamental Orders, Connecticut was granted governmental authority by King Charles II of England through the Connecticut Charter of 1662.

name: connecticut
sentence: Separate branches of government did not exist during this period, and the General Assembly acted as the supreme authority.

name: connecticut
sentence: A constitution similar to the modern US Constitution was not adopted in Connecticut until 1818.

name: connecticut
sentence: Finally, the current state constitution was implemented in 1965.

name: connecticut
sentence: The 1965 constitution absorbed a majority of its 1818 predecessor, but incorporated a handful of important modifications.

name: connecticut
sentence: The governor heads the executive branch.

name: connecticut
sentence: As of 2020, Ned Lamont is the Governor and Susan Bysiewicz is the Lieutenant Governor; both are Democrats.

name: connecticut
sentence: From 1639 until the adoption of the 1818 constitution, the governor presided over the General Assembly.

name: connecticut
sentence: In 1974, Ella Grasso was elected as the governor of Connecticut.

name: connecticut
sentence: This was the first time in United States history when a woman was a governor without her husband being governor first.There are several executive departments: Administrative Services, Agriculture, Banking, Children and Families, Consumer Protection, Correction, Economic and Community Development, Developmental Services, Construction Services, Education, Emergency Management and Public Protection, Energy & Environmental Protection, Higher Education, Insurance, Labor, Mental Health and Addiction Services, Military, Motor Vehicles, Public Health, Public Utility Regulatory Authority, Public Works, Revenue Services, Social Services, Transportation, and Veterans Affairs.

name: connecticut
sentence: In addition to these departments, there are other independent bureaus, offices and commissions.In addition to the Governor and Lieutenant Governor, there are four other executive officers named in the state constitution that are elected directly by voters: Secretary of the State, Treasurer, Comptroller, and Attorney General.

name: connecticut
sentence: All executive officers are elected to four-year terms.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut's legislative branch is known as the General Assembly.

name: connecticut
sentence: It is a bicameral legislature consisting of an upper body, the State Senatorte (36 senators); and a lower body, the House of Representatives (151 representatives).

name: connecticut
sentence: Bills must pass each house in order to become law.

name: connecticut
sentence: The governor can veto bills, but this veto can be overridden by a two-thirds majority in both houses.

name: connecticut
sentence: Per Article XV of the state constitution, Senatortors and Representatives must be at least 18 years of age and are elected to two-year terms in November on even-numbered years.

name: connecticut
sentence: There also must always be between 30 and 50 senators and 125 to 225 representatives.

name: connecticut
sentence: The Lieutenant Governor presides over the Senatorte, except when absent from the chamber, when the President pro tempore presides.

name: connecticut
sentence: The Speaker of the House presides over the House.

name: connecticut
sentence: As of 2021, Matthew Ritter is the Speaker of the House of Connecticut.

name: connecticut
sentence: As of 2021, Connecticut's United States Senatortors are Richard Blumenthal (Democrat) and Chris Murphy (Democrat).

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut has five representatives in the US House, all of whom are Democrats.Locally elected representatives also develop local ordinances to govern cities and towns.

name: connecticut
sentence: The town ordinances often include noise control and zoning guidelines.

name: connecticut
sentence: However, the State of Connecticut also provides statewide ordinances for noise control as well.

name: connecticut
sentence: The highest court of Connecticut's judicial branch is the Connecticut Supreme Court, headed by the Chief Justice of Connecticut.

name: connecticut
sentence: The Supreme Court is responsible for deciding on the constitutionality of laws, or cases as they relate to the law.

name: connecticut
sentence: Its proceedings are similar to those of the United States Supreme Court: no testimony is given by witnesses, and the lawyers of the two sides each present oral arguments no longer than thirty minutes.

name: connecticut
sentence: Following a court proceeding, the court may take several months to arrive at a judgment.

name: connecticut
sentence: As of 2020, the Chief Justice is Richard A. Robinson.

name: connecticut
sentence: In 1818, the court became a separate entity, independent of the legislative and executive branches.

name: connecticut
sentence: The Connecticut Appellate Court is a lesser statewide court, and the Superior Courts are lower courts that resemble county courts of other states.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut does not have county government, unlike all other states except Rhode Island.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut county governments were mostly eliminated in 1960, with the exception of sheriffs elected in each county.

name: connecticut
sentence: In 2000, the county sheriff was abolished and replaced with the state marshal system, which has districts that follow the old county territories.

name: connecticut
sentence: The judicial system is divided into judicial districts at the trial-court level which largely follow the old county lines.

name: connecticut
sentence: The eight counties are still widely used for purely geographical and statistical purposes, such as weather reports and census reporting.

name: connecticut
sentence: The state is divided into nine regional councils of government defined by the state Office of Planning and Management, which facilitate regional planning and coordination of services between member towns.

name: connecticut
sentence: The Intragovernmental Policy Division of this Office coordinates regional planning with the administrative bodies of these regions.

name: connecticut
sentence: Each region has an administrative body made up chief executive officers of the member towns.

name: connecticut
sentence: The regions are established for the purpose of planning "coordination of regional and state planning activities; redesignation of logical planning regions and promotion of the continuation of regional planning organizations within the state; and provision for technical aid and the administration of financial assistance to regional planning organizations".

name: connecticut
sentence: By 2015, the State of Connecticut recognized COGs as county equivalents, allowing them to apply for funding and grants made available to county governments in other states.

name: connecticut
sentence: In 2019 the state recommended to the United States Census Bureau that the nine Councils of Governments replace its counties for statistical purposes.

name: connecticut
sentence: This proposal was approved by the Census Bureau in 2022, and will be fully implemented by 2024.Connecticut shares with the rest of New England a governmental institution called the New England town.

name: connecticut
sentence: The state is divided into 169 towns which serve as the fundamental political jurisdictions.

name: connecticut
sentence: There are also 21 cities, most of which simply follow the boundaries of their namesake towns and have a merged city-town government.

name: connecticut
sentence: There are two exceptions: the City of Groton, which is a subsection of the Town of Groton, and the City of Winsted in the Town of Winchester.

name: connecticut
sentence: There are also nine incorporated boroughs which may provide additional services to a section of town.

name: connecticut
sentence: Naugatuck is a consolidated town and borough.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut is generally considered to be a blue state.

name: connecticut
sentence: The last Republican presidential candidate to win Connecticut's votes in the Electoral College was George H W Bush in 1988.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut residents who register to vote may declare an affiliation to a political party, may become unaffiliated at will, and may change affiliations subject to certain waiting periods.

name: connecticut
sentence: As of 2022 around 58% of registered voters are enrolled in a political party.

name: connecticut
sentence: The Democratic Party of Connecticut is the largest party in the state by voter registration, with 36% of voters, followed by the Connecticut Republican Party with approximately 20%.

name: connecticut
sentence: An additional 1.6% are registered to third parties.

name: connecticut
sentence: As of 2022, 4 third parties have statewide enrollment privileges (meaning any state resident may register as a member), including the Libertarian Party of Connecticut, the Independent Party of Connecticut, the Connecticut Green Party, and the Connecticut Working Families Party.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut allows electoral fusion, where the same candidate can run on the ballot of more than one political party; this is often used by the Connecticut Working Families Party to cross-endorse Democratic candidates.

name: connecticut
sentence: In July 2009, the Connecticut legislature overrode a veto by Governor M. Jodi Rell to pass SustiNet, the first significant public-option health care reform legislation in the nation.In April 2012, both houses of the Connecticut state legislature passed a bill (20 to 16 and 86 to 62) that abolished capital punishment for all future crimes, while 11 inmates who were waiting on the death row at the time could still be executed.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut ranked third in the nation for educational performance, according to Education Week's Quality Counts 2018 report.

name: connecticut
sentence: It earned an overall score of 83.5 out of 100 points.

name: connecticut
sentence: On average, the country received a score of 75.2.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut posted a B-plus in the Chance-for-Success category, ranking fourth on factors that contribute to a person's success both within and outside the K-12 education system.

name: connecticut
sentence: Connecticut received a mark of B-plus and finished fourth for School Finance.

name: connecticut
sentence: It ranked 12th with a grade of C on the K-12 Achievement Index.

name: connecticut
sentence: Hartford Public High School (1638) is the third-oldest secondary school in the nation after the Collegiate School (1628) in Manhattan and the Boston Latin School (1635).

name: connecticut
sentence: Today, the Connecticut State Board of Education manages the public school system for children in grades K–12.

name: connecticut

sentence: The Woodland period ended around 1000 AD.The Mississippian culture emerged, lasting from 1000 AD until the 15th century, shortly before the arrival of Europeans.

sentence: Mississippian civilization collapsed in Indiana during the mid-15th century for reasons that remain unclear.The historic Native American tribes in the area at the time of European encounter spoke different languages of the Algonquian family.

sentence: Echoing historical trends, the state has increasingly re-urbanized, with growth in cities outpacing suburbs since 2008.New Jersey is one of the wealthiest states in the US, consistently ranking as one of the top three by median household income.

name: new_jersey
sentence: As glaciers retreated, they left behind Lake Passaic along with rivers, grasslands, swamps, and gorges.Since the 6th millennium BC, Native American people have inhabited New Jersey, beginning with the Lenape tribe.

sentence: The Lenape were several autonomous groups that practiced maize agriculture in order to supplement their hunting and gathering in the region surrounding the Delaware River, the lower Hudson River, and western Long Island Sound.

sentence: The Lenape were divided into matrilinear clans that were based upon common female ancestors.

name: north_carolina
sentence: The earliest evidence of human occupation in North Carolina dates back 10,000 years, found at the Hardaway Site.

name: north_carolina
sentence: King Charles II granted eight lord proprietors a colony they named Carolina after the king and which was established in 1670 with the first permanent settlement at Charles Town (Charleston).

sentence: In 1755, colonial North Carolina received its first postmaster, James Davis, appointed by Benjamin Franklin.

sentence: The Halifax Resolves resolution adopted by North Carolina on April 12, 1776, was the first formal call for independence from Great Britain among the American Colonies during the American Revolution.On November 21, 1789, North Carolina became the 12th state to ratify the United States Constitution.

name: north_carolina
sentence: In the run-up to the American Civil War, North Carolina declared its secession from the Union on May 20, 1861, becoming the tenth of eleven states to join the Confederate States of America.

sentence: Following the Civil War, the state was restored to the Union on July 4, 1868.

sentence: On December 17, 1903, Orville and Wilbur Wright successfully piloted the world's first controlled, sustained flight of a powered, heavier-than-air aircraft at Kitty Hawk in North Carolina's Outer Banks.

sentence: North Carolina often uses the slogan "First in Flight" on state license plates to commemorate this achievement, alongside a newer alternative design bearing the slogan "First in Freedom" in reference to the Mecklenburg Declaration and Halifax Resolves.

name: north_carolina
sentence: North Carolina is defined by a wide range of elevations and landscapes.

name: north_carolina
sentence: North Carolina's Mount Mitchell at 6,684 ft (2,037 m) is the highest point in North America east of the Mississippi River.

name: north_carolina
sentence: Most of the state falls in the humid subtropical climate zone; however, the western, mountainous part of the state has a subtropical highland climate.

name: north_carolina
sentence: North Carolina was inhabited for at least 10,000 years by succeeding prehistoric indigenous cultures.

name: north_carolina
sentence: The Hardaway Site saw major periods of occupation dating to 10,000 years BCE.

name: north_carolina
sentence: Before 200 AD, the people were building earthwork platform mounds, which were used for ceremonial and religious purposes.

name: north_carolina
sentence: Succeeding peoples, including those of the South Appalachian Mississippian culture, established by 1000 AD in the Piedmont and mountain region, continued to build this style of mounds.

name: north_carolina
sentence: In contrast to some of the larger centers of the classic Mississippian culture (as noted below), in what became known as the western Carolinas, northeastern Georgia and southeastern Tennessee, most of the larger towns had only one central platform mound.

name: north_carolina
sentence: The smaller settlements had none but developed close to the more prominent towns.

name: north_carolina
sentence: This area became known as the homelands of the historic Cherokee people, who are believed to have migrated over time from the Great Lakes area.

name: north_carolina
sentence: In the 500–700 years preceding European contact, the Mississippian culture built elaborate cities and maintained far-flung regional trading networks.

name: north_carolina
sentence: Its largest city was Cahokia, which had numerous mounds for different purposes, a highly stratified society, and was located in present-day southwestern Illinois near the Mississippi River.

name: north_carolina
sentence: The Native polities of the Mississippian culture fell apart and reformed as new groups, such as the Catawba, due to a series of destabilizing events known as the "Mississippian shatter zone".

name: north_carolina
sentence: Introduction of colonial trading arrangements and hostile native groups from the north such as the Westo Indians hastened changes in an already tenuous regional hierarchy.

name: north_carolina
sentence: As described by anthropologist Robbie Ethridge, the Mississippian shatter zone was an area of great instability, in what is now the American South, caused by the instability of Mississippian chiefdoms, high mortality from new Eurasian diseases, conversion to an agricultural society and the accompanying population increase, and the emergence of Native "militaristic slaving societies".Historically documented tribes in the North Carolina region include the Carolina Algonquian-speaking tribes of the coastal areas, such as the Chowanoke, Roanoke, Pamlico, Machapunga, and Coree, who were the first encountered by the English; the Iroquoian-speaking Meherrin, Cherokee, and Tuscarora of the interior; and Southeastern Siouan tribes, such as the Cheraw, Waxhaw, Saponi, Waccamaw, Cape Fear Indians, and Catawba of the Piedmont.

name: north_carolina
sentence: In the late 16th century, the first Spanish explorers traveling inland recorded meeting Mississippian culture people at Joara, a regional chiefdom near what later developed as Morganton.

name: north_carolina
sentence: In 1567, Captain Juan Pardo led an expedition to claim the area for the Spanish colony and to establish another route to reach silver mines in Mexico.

sentence: Pardo made a winter base at Joara, which he renamed Cuenca.

name: north_carolina
sentence: His expedition built Fort San Juan and left a contingent of 30 Spaniards there, while Pardo traveled further.

name: north_carolina
sentence: He returned by a different route to Santa Elena on Parris Island, South Carolina, then a center of Spanish Florida.

sentence: In the spring of 1568, natives killed all but one of the Spaniards and burned the six forts in the interior, including the one at Fort San Juan.

sentence: Although the Spanish never returned to the interior, this effort marked the first European attempt at colonization of the interior of what became the United States.

name: north_carolina
sentence: A 16th-century journal by Pardo's scribe Bandera, and archaeological findings since 1986 at Joara, have confirmed the settlement.

name: north_carolina
sentence: In 1584, Elizabeth I granted a charter to Sir Walter Raleigh, for whom the state capital is named, for land in present-day North Carolina (then part of the territory of Virginia).

sentence: Manteo was also the first indigenous North American to be baptized by English settlers.

sentence: Upon White's return in 1590, neither native nor Englishman were to be found.

sentence: Popular theory holds that the colonists either traveled away with or assimilated into local native culture.

sentence: Virginia Dare, the first English person to be born in North America, was born on Roanoke Island on August 18, 1587; the surrounding Dare County is named for her.

sentence: In 1712 owing to disputes over governance, the Carolina colony split into North Carolina and South Carolina.

sentence: North Carolina would become a crown colony in 1729.Most of the English colonists had arrived as indentured servants, hiring themselves out as laborers for a fixed period to pay for their passage.

sentence: Unable to establish deep water ports such as at Charles Town and Norfolk, the economy's growth and prosperity was thus based on cheap labor and slave plantation systems, devoted primarily to the production of tobacco, then later cotton and textiles.In 1738–1739, smallpox would cause high fatalities among the Native Americans, who had no immunity to the new disease (it had become endemic over centuries in Europe).

sentence: Except for the Earl Granville holdings, it became a royal colony seventeen years later.In June 1718, the pirate Blackbeard ran his flagship, the Queen Anne's Revenge, aground at Beaufort Inlet, North Carolina, in present-day Carteret County.
