sentence: In 1996, Intersal, Inc., a private firm, discovered the remains of a vessel likely to be the Queen Anne's Revenge, which was added to the US National Register of Historic Places.North Carolina became one of the Thirteen Colonies and with the territory of South Carolina was originally known as the Province of North Carolina.

sentence: Loyalists in North Carolina were smaller in number than in some other colonies such as Georgia, South Carolina, Delaware, and New York.During colonial times, Edenton served as the state capital beginning in 1722, followed by New Bern becoming the capital in 1766.

sentence: Construction of Tryon Palace, which served as the residence and offices of the provincial governor William Tryon, began in 1767 and was completed in 1771.

name: north_carolina
sentence: The population of the colony more than quadrupled from 52,000 in 1740 to 270,000 in 1780 from high immigration from Virginia, Maryland and Pennsylvania, plus immigrants from abroad.North Carolina did not have any printer or print shops until 1749, when the North Carolina Assembly commissioned James Davis from Williamsburg Virginia to act as their official printer.

name: north_carolina
sentence: Before this time the laws and legal journals of North Carolina were handwritten and were largely kept in a disorganized manner, prompting them to hire Davis.

sentence: He was also active in North Carolina's politics, as a member of the Assembly and later as the Sheriff.

name: north_carolina
sentence: Davis also founded and printed the North-Carolina Gazette, North Carolina's first newspaper, printed in his printing house in New Bern.Differences in the settlement patterns of eastern and western North Carolina, or the Atlantic coastal plain and uplands, affected the political, economic, and social life of the state from the 18th until the 20th century.

sentence: Eastern North Carolina was settled chiefly by immigrants from rural England and Gaelic speakers from the Scottish Highlands.

sentence: Arriving during the mid-to-late 18th century, the Scots-Irish, people of Scottish descent who migrated to and then emigrated from what is today Northern Ireland, were the largest non-English immigrant group before the Revolution; English indentured servants were overwhelmingly the largest immigrant group before the Revolution.

name: north_carolina
sentence: During the American Revolutionary War, the English and Gaelic speaking Highland Scots of eastern North Carolina tended to remain loyal to the British Crown, because of longstanding business and personal connections with Great Britain.

name: north_carolina

sentence: In some cases the war was also an excuse to settle private grudges and rivalries.North Carolina had around 7,800 Patriots join the Continental Army under General George Washington; and an additional 10,000 served in local militia units under such leaders as General Nathanael Greene.

name: north_carolina
sentence: It ceded them to the national government so the Northwest Territory could be organized and managed nationally.A major American victory in the war took place at King's Mountain along the North Carolina–South Carolina border; on October 7, 1780, a force of 1,000 Patriots from western North Carolina (including what is today the state of Tennessee) and southwest Virginia overwhelmed a force of some 1,000 British troops led by Major Patrick Ferguson.

name: north_carolina
sentence: Most of the soldiers fighting for the British side in this battle were Carolinians who had remained loyal to the Crown (they were called "Tories" or Loyalists).

sentence: The road to Yorktown and America's independence from Great Britain led through North Carolina.

sentence: As the British Army moved north from victories in Charleston and Camden, South Carolina, the Southern Division of the Continental Army and local militia prepared to meet them.

name: north_carolina
sentence: Following General Daniel Morgan's victory over the British Cavalry Commander Banastre Tarleton at the Battle of Cowpens on January 17, 1781, southern commander Nathanael Greene led British Lord Charles Cornwallis across the heartland of North Carolina, and away from the latter's base of supply in Charleston, South Carolina.

name: north_carolina
sentence: This campaign is known as "The Race to the Dan" or "The Race for the River".In the Battle of Cowan's Ford, Cornwallis met resistance along the banks of the Catawba River at Cowan's Ford on February 1, 1781, in an attempt to engage General Morgan's forces during a tactical withdrawal.

name: north_carolina
sentence: Morgan had moved to the northern part of the state to combine with General Greene's newly recruited forces.

name: north_carolina
sentence: Although the British troops held the field at the end of the battle, their casualties at the hands of the numerically superior Continental Army were crippling.

sentence: Most were descendants from free African Americans who had migrated along with neighbors from Virginia during the 18th century.

sentence: The majority were the descendants of unions in the working classes between white women, indentured servants or free, and African men, indentured, slave or free.

name: north_carolina
sentence: After the American Revolution, Quakers and Mennonites worked to persuade slaveholders to free their slaves.

name: north_carolina
sentence: Some were inspired by their efforts and the language of the Revolution to arrange for manumission of their slaves.

name: north_carolina
sentence: The number of free people of color rose markedly in the first couple of decades after the Revolution.

name: north_carolina
sentence: Many free people of color migrated to the frontier, along with their European-American neighbors, where the social system was looser.

name: north_carolina
sentence: By 1810, nearly three percent of the free population consisted of free people of color, who numbered slightly more than 10,000.

name: north_carolina
sentence: The western areas of North Carolina were mainly white families of European descent, especially Scotch-Irish, who operated small subsistence farms.

name: north_carolina
sentence: In the early national period, the state became a center of Jeffersonian and Jacksonian democracy, with a strong Whig presence, especially in the western part of the state.

name: north_carolina
sentence: After Nat Turner's slave uprising in 1831, North Carolina and other southern states reduced the rights of free blacks.

name: north_carolina
sentence: In 1835, the legislature withdrew their right to vote.

name: north_carolina
sentence: In mid-century, the state's rural and commercial areas were connected by the construction of a 129 mi (208 km) wooden plank road, known as a "farmer's railroad", from Fayetteville in the east to Bethania (northwest of Winston-Salem).

name: north_carolina
sentence: On October 25, 1836, construction began on the Wilmington and Raleigh Railroad to connect the port city of Wilmington with the state capital of Raleigh.

name: north_carolina
sentence: In 1840, the state capitol building in Raleigh was completed, and still stands today.

name: north_carolina
sentence: In 1849, the North Carolina Railroad was created by act of the legislature to extend that railroad west to Greensboro, High Point, and Charlotte.

name: north_carolina
sentence: During the Civil War, the Wilmington-to-Raleigh stretch of the railroad would be vital to the Confederate war effort; supplies shipped into Wilmington would be moved by rail through Raleigh to the Confederate capital of Richmond, Virginia.

name: north_carolina
sentence: In 1860, North Carolina was a slave state, in which one-third of the state's total population were African-American slaves.

name: north_carolina
sentence: The state did not vote to join the Confederacy until President Abraham Lincoln called on it to invade its sister state, South Carolina, becoming the last or penultimate state to officially join the Confederacy.

name: north_carolina
sentence: The title of "last to join the Confederacy" has been disputed; although Tennessee's informal secession on May 7, 1861, preceded North Carolina's official secession on May 20, the Tennessee legislature did not formally vote to secede until June 8, 1861.Around 125,000 troops from North Carolina served in the Confederate Army, and about 15,000 North Carolina troops (both black and white) served in Union Army regiments, including those who left the state to join Union regiments elsewhere.

sentence: Over 30,000 North Carolina troops died from combat or disease during the war.

sentence: Confederate troops from all parts of North Carolina served in virtually all the major battles of the Army of Northern Virginia, the Confederacy's most famous army.

sentence: The first Confederate soldier to be killed in the Civil War was Private Henry Wyatt from North Carolina, in the Battle of Big Bethel in June 1861.

name: north_carolina
sentence: At the Battle of Gettysburg in July 1863, the 26th North Carolina Regiment participated in Pickett/Pettigrew's Charge and advanced the farthest into Union lines of any Confederate regiment.

name: north_carolina
sentence: The phrase "First at Bethel, Farthest at Gettysburg and Chickamauga, and Last at Appomattox", later became used through much of the early 20th century.After secession, some North Carolinians refused to support the Confederacy.

sentence: Numerous slaves would also escape to Union lines, where they became essentially free.

name: north_carolina
sentence: Following the collapse of the Confederacy in 1865, North Carolina, along with other former Confederate States (except Tennessee), was put under direct control by the US military and was relieved of its constitutional government and representation within the United States Congress in what is now referred to as the Reconstruction era.

name: north_carolina
sentence: In order to earn back its rights, the state had to make concessions to Washington, one of which was ratifying the Thirteenth Amendment.

name: north_carolina
sentence: Congressional Republicans during Reconstruction, commonly referred to as "radical Republicans", constantly pushed for new constitutions for each of the Southern states that emphasized equal rights for African-Americans.

name: north_carolina
sentence: In 1868, a constitutional convention restored the state government of North Carolina.

name: north_carolina
sentence: Though the Fifteenth Amendment was also adopted that same year, it remained in most cases ineffective for almost a century, not to mention paramilitary groups and their lynching with impunity.The elections in April 1868 following the constitutional convention led to a narrow victory for a Republican-dominated government, with 19 African-Americans holding positions in the North Carolina State Legislature.

name: north_carolina
sentence: In attempt to put the reforms into effect, the new Republican Governor William W. Holden declared martial law on any county allegedly not complying with law and order using the passage of the Shoffner Act.

name: north_carolina
sentence: A Republican Party coalition of black freedmen, northern carpetbaggers and local scalawags controlled state government for three years.

name: north_carolina
sentence: The white conservative Democrats regained control of the state legislature in 1870, in part by Ku Klux Klan violence and terrorism at the polls, to suppress black voting.

name: north_carolina
sentence: Republicans were elected to the governorship until 1876, when the Red Shirts, a paramilitary organization that arose in 1874 and was allied with the Democratic Party, helped suppress black voting.

name: north_carolina
sentence: More than 150 black Americans were murdered in electoral violence in 1876.

sentence: Post civil war-debt cycles pushed people to switch from subsistence agriculture to commodity agriculture.

sentence: Democrats were elected to the legislature and governor's office, but the Populists attracted voters displeased with them.

sentence: In 1896 a biracial, Populist-Republican Fusionist coalition gained the governor's office and passed laws that would extend the voting franchise to blacks and poor whites.

sentence: The Democrats regained control of the legislature in 1896 and passed laws to impose Jim Crow and racial segregation of public facilities.

Waddell as mayor, in the only successful coup d'état in United States history.In 1899, the state legislature passed a new constitution, with requirements for poll taxes and literacy tests for voter registration which disenfranchised most black Americans in the state.

sentence: North Carolina is bordered by South Carolina on the south, Georgia on the southwest, Tennessee on the west, Virginia on the north, and the Atlantic Ocean on the east.

name: north_carolina
sentence: The United States Census Bureau places North Carolina in the South Atlantic division of the southern region.North Carolina consists of three main geographic regions: the Atlantic coastal plain, occupying the eastern portion of the state; the central Piedmont region, and the mountain region in the west, which is part of the Appalachian Mountains.

name: north_carolina
sentence: The coastal plain consists of more specifically-defined areas known as the Outer Banks, a string of sandy, narrow barrier islands separated from the mainland by sounds or inlets, including Albemarle Sound and Pamlico Sound, the native home of the venus flytrap, and the inner coastal plain, where longleaf pine trees are native.

name: north_carolina
sentence: So many ships have been lost off Cape Hatteras that the area is known as the "Graveyard of the Atlantic"; more than a thousand ships have sunk in these waters since records began in 1526.

name: north_carolina
sentence: The most famous of these is the Queen Anne's Revenge (flagship of the pirate Blackbeard), which went aground in Beaufort Inlet in 1718.The coastal plain transitions to the Piedmont region along the Atlantic Seaboard fall line, the elevation at which waterfalls first appear on streams and rivers.

name: north_carolina
sentence: The Piedmont region of central North Carolina is the state's most populous region, containing the six largest cities in the state by population.

name: north_carolina
sentence: It consists of gently rolling countryside frequently broken by hills or low mountain ridges.

name: north_carolina
sentence: Small, isolated, and deeply eroded mountain ranges and peaks are located in the Piedmont, including the Sauratown Mountains, Pilot Mountain, the Uwharrie Mountains, Crowder's Mountain, King's Pinnacle, the Brushy Mountains, and the South Mountains.

name: north_carolina
sentence: The Piedmont ranges from about 300 feet (91 m) in elevation in the east to about 1,500 feet (460 m) in the west.

name: north_carolina
sentence: The western section of the state is part of the Blue Ridge Mountains of the larger Appalachian Mountain range.

name: north_carolina
sentence: Among the subranges of the Blue Ridge Mountains located in the state are the Great Smoky Mountains and the Black Mountains.

name: north_carolina
sentence: The Black Mountains are the highest in the eastern United States, and culminate in Mount Mitchell at 6,684 feet (2,037 m), the highest point east of the Mississippi River.

name: north_carolina
sentence: North Carolina has 17 major river basins.

name: north_carolina
sentence: The five basins west of the Blue Ridge Mountains flow to the Gulf of Mexico, while the remainder flow to the Atlantic Ocean.

name: north_carolina
sentence: Of the 17 basins, 11 originate within the state of North Carolina, but only four are contained entirely within the state's border—the Cape Fear, the Neuse, the White Oak, and the Tar–Pamlico basin.

name: north_carolina
sentence: Elevation above sea level is most responsible for temperature change across the state, with the mountainous regions being coolest year-round.

name: north_carolina
sentence: The climate is also influenced by the Atlantic Ocean and the Gulf Stream, especially in the coastal plain.

name: north_carolina
sentence: These influences tend to cause warmer winter temperatures along the coast, where temperatures only occasionally drop below the freezing point at night.

name: north_carolina
sentence: The coastal plain averages around 1 inch (2.5 cm) of snow or ice annually, and in many years, there may be no snow or ice at all.The Atlantic Ocean exerts less influence on the climate of the Piedmont region, which has hotter summers and colder winters than along the coast, though winters are still mild.North Carolina experiences severe weather both in summer and in winter, with summer bringing threat of hurricanes, tropical storms, heavy rain, and flooding.

name: north_carolina
sentence: Destructive hurricanes that have hit North Carolina include Hurricane Fran, Hurricane Florence, Hurricane Floyd, Hurricane Hugo, and Hurricane Hazel, the latter being the strongest storm ever to make landfall in the state, as a Category 4 in 1954.

name: north_carolina
sentence: Hurricane Isabel ranks as the most destructive of the 21st century.North Carolina averages fewer than 20 tornadoes per year, many of them produced by hurricanes or tropical storms along the coastal plain.

name: north_carolina
sentence: Tornadoes from thunderstorms are a risk, especially in the eastern part of the state.

name: north_carolina
sentence: The western Piedmont is often protected by the mountains, which tend to break up storms as they try to cross over; the storms will often re-form farther east.

sentence: A phenomenon known as "cold-air damming" often occurs in the northwestern part of the state, which can weaken storms but can also lead to major ice events in winter.In April 2011, the worst tornado outbreak in North Carolina's history occurred.

sentence: North Carolina provides a large range of recreational activities, from swimming at the beach to skiing in the mountains.

sentence: North Carolina has theme parks, aquariums, museums, historic sites, lighthouses, elegant theaters, concert halls, and fine dining.North Carolinians enjoy outdoor recreation utilizing numerous local bike paths, 34 state parks, and 14 national parks.

sentence: North Carolina residents since the colonial era have historically been overwhelmingly Protestant—first Anglican, then Baptist and Methodist.

name: ohio
sentence: Ohio, officially the State of Ohio ( (listen)) is a state in the Midwestern United States.

name: ohio
sentence: Of the fifty US states, it is the 34th-largest by area.

name: ohio
sentence: With a population of nearly 11.8 million, Ohio is the seventh-most populous and tenth-most densely populated state.

name: ohio
sentence: Its capital and largest city is Columbus, with the Columbus metro area, Greater Cincinnati, and Greater Cleveland being the largest metropolitan areas.

name: ohio
sentence: Ohio is bordered by Lake Erie to the north, Pennsylvania to the east, West Virginia to the southeast, Kentucky to the southwest, Indiana to the west, and Michigan to the northwest.

name: ohio
sentence: Ohio is nicknamed the "Buckeye State" after its Ohio buckeye trees, and Ohioans are also known as "Buckeyes".

name: ohio
sentence: Its state flag is the only non-rectangular flag of all the US states.

name: ohio
sentence: Ohio takes its name from the Ohio River, which, in turn, originated from the Senatorca word ohiːyo', meaning "good river", "great river", or "large creek".

name: ohio
sentence: The state arose from the lands west of the Appalachian Mountains that were contested from colonial times through the Northwest Indian Wars of the late 18th century.

name: ohio
sentence: It was partitioned from the resulting Northwest Territory, which was the first frontier of the new United States, becoming the 17th state admitted to the Union on March 1, 1803, and the first under the Northwest Ordinance.

name: ohio
sentence: Ohio was the first post-colonial free state admitted to the union and became one of the earliest and most influential industrial powerhouses during the 20th century.

name: ohio
sentence: Although it has transitioned to a more information- and service-based economy in the 21st century, it remains an industrial state, ranking seventh in GDP as of 2019, with the third-largest manufacturing sector and second-largest automobile production.The government of Ohio is composed of the executive branch, led by the governor; the legislative branch, consisting of the bicameral Ohio General Assembly; and the judicial branch, led by the state Supreme Court.

name: ohio
sentence: Ohio occupies 16 seats in the United States House of Representatives.

name: ohio
sentence: The state is known for its status as both a swing state and a bellwether in national elections.

name: ohio
sentence: Seven presidents of the United States have come from Ohio.

name: ohio
sentence: This has led to it receiving the moniker "the Mother of Presidents".

name: ohio
sentence: Archeological evidence of spear points of both the Folsom and Clovis types indicate that the Ohio Valley was inhabited by nomadic people as early as 13,000 BC.

name: ohio
sentence: These early nomads disappeared from Ohio by 1,000 BC.

name: ohio
sentence: Between 1,000 and 800 BC, the sedentary Adena culture emerged.

name: ohio
sentence: The Adena were able to establish "semi-permanent" villages because they domesticated plants, including sunflowers, and "grew squash and possibly corn"; with hunting and gathering, this cultivation supported more settled, complex villages.

name: ohio
sentence: The most notable remnant of the Adena culture is the Great Serpent Mound, located in Adams County, Ohio.Around 100 BC, the Adena evolved into the Hopewell people who were also mound builders.

name: ohio
sentence: Their complex, large and technologically sophisticated earthworks can be found in modern-day Marietta, Newark, and Circleville.

name: ohio
sentence: They were also a prolific trading society, their trading network spanning a third of the continent.

name: ohio
sentence: The Hopewell disappeared from the Ohio Valley about 600 AD.

name: ohio
sentence: The Mississippian culture rose as the Hopewell culture declined.

name: ohio
sentence: Many Siouan-speaking peoples from the plains and east coast claim them as ancestors and say they lived throughout the Ohio region until approximately the 13th century.There were three other cultures contemporaneous with the Mississippians: the Fort Ancient people, the Whittlesey focus people and the Monongahela Culture.

name: ohio
sentence: All three cultures disappeared in the 17th century.

name: ohio
sentence: Their origins are unknown.

name: ohio
sentence: The Shawnees may have absorbed the Fort Ancient people.

name: ohio
sentence: It is also possible that the Monongahela held no land in Ohio during the Colonial Era.

name: ohio
sentence: The Mississippian culture was close to and traded extensively with the Fort Ancient people.

name: ohio
sentence: Indians in the Ohio Valley were greatly affected by the aggressive tactics of the Iroquois Confederation, based in central and western New York.

name: ohio
sentence: After the Beaver Wars in the mid-17th century, the Iroquois claimed much of the Ohio country as hunting and, more importantly, beaver-trapping ground.

name: ohio
sentence: After the devastation of epidemics and war in the mid-17th century, which largely emptied the Ohio country of indigenous people by the mid-to-late 17th century, the land gradually became repopulated by the mostly Algonquian.

name: ohio
sentence: Many of these Ohio-country nations were multi-ethnic (sometimes multi-linguistic) societies born out of the earlier devastation brought about by disease, war, and subsequent social instability.

name: ohio
sentence: They subsisted on agriculture (corn, sunflowers, beans, etc.)

name: ohio
sentence: supplemented by seasonal hunts.

name: ohio
sentence: By the 18th century, they were part of a larger global economy brought about by European entry into the fur trade.Some of the indigenous nations which historically inhabited Ohio included the Iroquoian, the Algonquian and the Siouan.

name: ohio
sentence: Ohio country was also the site of Indian massacres, such as the Yellow Creek massacre, the Gnadenhutten massacre and the Enoch Brown school massacre.

name: ohio
sentence: After the War of 1812, when Natives suffered serious losses such as at Tippecanoe, most Native tribes either left Ohio or had to live on only limited reservations.

name: ohio
sentence: By 1842, all remaining Natives were forced out of the state.

name: ohio
sentence: During the 18th century, the French set up a system of trading posts to control the fur trade in the region.

name: ohio
sentence: Beginning in 1754, the Kingdom of France and Kingdom of Great Britain fought in the French and Indian War, with various Native American tribes on each side.

name: ohio
sentence: As a result of the Treaty of Paris, the French ceded control of Ohio and the remainder of the Old Northwest to Great Britain in 1763.Prior to the American Revolution, Britain thinly exercised sovereignty over Ohio Country by lackadaisical garrisoning of the French forts.

name: ohio
sentence: Just beyond Ohio Country was the great Miami capital of Kekionga which became the center of British trade and influence in Ohio Country and throughout the future Northwest Territory.

name: ohio
sentence: By the Royal Proclamation of 1763, British lands west of Appalachia were forbidden to settlement by colonists.

name: ohio
sentence: The Treaty of Fort Stanwix in 1768 explicitly reserved lands north and west of the Ohio as Native lands.

name: ohio
sentence: British military occupation in the region contributed to the outbreak of Pontiac's War in 1763.

name: ohio
sentence: Ohio tribes participated in the war until an armed expedition in Ohio led by Colonel Henry Bouquet brought about a truce.

name: ohio
sentence: Another colonial military expedition into the Ohio Country in 1774 brought Lord Dunmore's War, kicked off by the Yellow Creek massacre in Ohio, to a conclusion.

name: ohio
sentence: In 1774, Britain passed the Quebec Act that formally annexed Ohio and other western lands to the Province of Quebec in order to provide a civil government and to centralize British administration of the Montreal-based fur trade.

name: ohio
sentence: The prohibition of settlement west of the Appalachians remained, contributing to the American Revolution.By the start of the American Revolutionary War, the movement of Natives and Americans between the Ohio Country and Thirteen Colonies had resulted in tension.

name: ohio
sentence: Fort Pitt in Pennsylvania had become the main fort where expeditions into Ohio started.

name: ohio
sentence: Intrusions into the area included General Edward Hand's 1778 movement of 500 Pennsylvania militiamen from Fort Pitt towards Mingo towns on the Cuyahoga River, where the British stored military supplies which they distributed to Indian raiding parties; Colonel Daniel Brodhead's invasion in 1780 and destruction of the Lenape Indian capital of Coshocton; a detachment of one hundred of George Rogers Clark's troops that were ambushed near the Ohio River by Indians led by Joseph Brant in the same year; a British and Native American attack on the US' Fort Laurens; and the 1782 detainment and murder of 96 Moravian Lenape pacifists by Pennsylvania militiamen in the Gnadenhutten massacre.The western theatre never had a decisive victor.

name: ohio
sentence: In the Treaty of Paris in 1783, Britain ceded all claims to Ohio Country to the new United States after its victory in the American Revolutionary War.

name: ohio
sentence: The United States created the Northwest Territory under the Northwest Ordinance of 1787.

name: ohio
sentence: Slavery was not permitted in the new territory.

name: ohio
sentence: Settlement began with the founding of Marietta by the Ohio Company of Associates, which had been formed by a group of American Revolutionary War veterans.

name: ohio
sentence: Following the Ohio Company, the Miami Company (also referred to as the "Symmes Purchase") claimed the southwestern section, and the Connecticut Land Company surveyed and settled the Connecticut Western Reserve in present-day Northeast Ohio.

name: ohio
sentence: Territorial surveyors from Fort Steuben began surveying an area of eastern Ohio called the Seven Ranges at about the same time.

name: ohio
sentence: The old Northwest Territory originally included areas previously known as Ohio Country and Illinois Country.

name: ohio
sentence: As Ohio prepared for statehood, the Indiana Territory was created, reducing the Northwest Territory to approximately the size of present-day Ohio plus the eastern half of the Lower Peninsula of Michigan and the eastern tip of the Upper Peninsula and a sliver of southeastern Indiana called "The Gore".

name: ohio
sentence: The coalition of Native American tribes, known as the Western Confederacy, was forced to cede extensive territory, including much of present-day Ohio, in the Treaty of Greenville in 1795.

sentence: Under the Northwest Ordinance, areas could be defined and admitted as states once their population reached 60,000.

sentence: Although Ohio's population was only 45,000 in December 1801, Congress determined that it was growing rapidly enough and accelerated the process via the Enabling Act of 1802.

sentence: Rufus Putnam served in important military capacities in both the French and Indian War and the American Revolutionary War.

sentence: He was one of the most highly respected men in the early years of the United States.In 1776, Putnam created a method of building portable fortifications, which enabled the Continental Army to drive the British from Boston.

sentence: Ultimately, after the United States government used the Indian Removal Act of 1830 to force countless Native American tribes on the Trail of Tears, where all the southern states except for Florida were successfully emptied of Native peoples, the US government panicked because a majority of tribes did not want to be forced out of their own lands.

name: ohio
sentence: Fearing further wars between Native tribes and American settlers, they pushed all remaining Native tribes in the East to migrate west against their own will, including all remaining tribes in Ohio.In 1835, Ohio fought with the Michigan Territory in the Toledo War, a mostly bloodless boundary war over the Toledo Strip.

sentence: Congress intervened, making Michigan's admittance as a state conditional on ending the conflict.

sentence: Discovery of coal deposits aided the further development of the steel industry in the state, and by 1853 Cleveland was the third largest iron and steel producer in the country.

sentence: Ohio was hit by its greatest natural disaster in the Great Flood of 1913, resulting in at least 428 fatalities and hundreds of millions of dollars in property damage, particularly around the Great Miami River basin.The National Football League was originally founded in Canton, Ohio in 1920 as the American Professional Football Conference.

sentence: Approximately 839,000 Ohioans served in the US armed forces during World War II, of which over 23,000 died or were missing in action.Artists, writers, musicians and actors developed in the state throughout the 20th century and often moved to other cities which were larger centers for their work.

sentence: Two Ohio astronauts completed significant milestones in the space race in the 1960s: John Glenn becoming the first American to orbit the Earth, and Neil Armstrong becoming the first human to walk on the Moon.

name: ohio
sentence: In 1967, Carl Stokes was elected mayor of Cleveland and became the first African American mayor of one of the nation's 10 most populous cities.In 1970, an Ohio Army National Guard unit fired at students during an anti-war protest at Kent State University, killing four and wounding nine.

sentence: The Guard had been called onto campus after several protests in and around campus had become violent, including a riot in downtown Kent and the burning of an ROTC building.

name: ohio
sentence: The main cause of the protests was the United States' invasion of Cambodia during the Vietnam War.Beginning in the 1980s, the state entered into international economic and resource cooperation treaties and organizations with other Midwestern states, as well as New York, Pennsylvania, Ontario, and Quebec, including the Great Lakes Charter, Great Lakes Compact, and the Council of Great Lakes Governors.

name: ohio
sentence: Ohio's economy has undergone significant change in the 21st century, as the trend of deindustrialization has greatly impacted the American Midwest and the Rust Belt.

sentence: Manufacturing in the Midwest experienced a stark decline during the early 21st century, a trend which greatly impacted Ohio.

name: ohio
sentence: From 1990 to 2019, Ohio lost over 300,000 manufacturing jobs, but added over 1,000,000 non-manufacturing jobs during that same time.

name: ohio
sentence: Coinciding with this decline, Ohio has seen a large decline in union membership: 17.4% of Ohioan workers were union members in 2000, while 12.8% were union members in 2022.In the wake of these economic changes, Ohio's state government has looked to promoting new industries to offset manufacturing losses, such as the production of solar energy and electric vehicles.

name: ohio
sentence: One major program launched by the state's government was the "Third Frontier" program, created during the governorship of Bob Taft, which aims to increase investment in Ohio, and boost the state's technology sector.

name: ohio
sentence: As of 2010, the Ohio Department of Development attributes the creation of 9,500 jobs to this program, with an average of salary of $65,000, while having a $6.6 billion economic impact with a return on investment of 9:1.

name: ohio
sentence: In 2010 the state won the International Economic Development Council's Excellence in Economic Development Award, celebrated as a national model of success.Many of the state's former industrial centers turned to new industries, including Akron as a center for polymer and biomedical research, Cincinnati as the state's largest mercantile hub, Columbus as a center for technological research and development, education, and insurance, Cleveland in regenerative medicine research and manufacturing, Dayton as an aerospace and defense hub, and Toledo as a national center for solar technology.Ohio's economy was also heavily afflicted by the Great Recession, as the state's unemployment rate rose from 5.6% in the first two months of 2008 up to a peak of 11.1% in December 2009 and January 2010.

name: ohio
sentence: It took until August 2014 for the unemployment rate to return to 5.6%.

sentence: The median household income dropped 7% from 2006-2007 to 2008-200, and the poverty rate ballooned to 13.5% by 2009.In 2015, Ohio gross domestic product was $608.1 billion, the seventh-largest economy among the 50 states.

sentence: In 2015, Ohio's total GDP accounted for 3.4% of US GDP and 0.8% of world GDP.Politically, Ohio has been long regarded as a swing state, however, the success of many Republican Party candidates in Ohio since the late 2000s has led many to question whether Ohio remains an electoral battleground.On March 9, 2020, the Covid-19 pandemic was confirmed to reach Ohio, with three cases being reported.

sentence: Ohio's economy was also heavily impacted by the pandemic, as the state saw large job losses in 2020, as well as large amounts of subsequent stimulus spending.

sentence: Ohio's geographic location has proven to be an asset for economic growth and expansion.

sentence: Because Ohio links the Northeast to the Midwest, much cargo and business traffic passes through its borders along its well-developed highways.

sentence: To the north, Ohio has 312 miles (502 km) of coastline with Lake Erie, which allows for numerous cargo ports such as Cleveland and Toledo.

sentence: Ohio's neighbors are Pennsylvania to the east, Michigan to the northwest, Lake Erie to the north, Indiana to the west, Kentucky on the south, and West Virginia on the southeast.

name: ohio
sentence: Ohio's borders were defined by metes and bounds in the Enabling Act of 1802 as follows: Bounded on the east by the Pennsylvania line, on the south by the Ohio River, to the mouth of the Great Miami River, on the west by the line drawn due north from the mouth of the Great Miami aforesaid, and on the north by an east and west line drawn through the southerly extreme of Lake Michigan, running east after intersecting the due north line aforesaid, from the mouth of the Great Miami until it shall intersect Lake Erie or the territorial line, and thence with the same through Lake Erie to the Pennsylvania line aforesaid.

sentence: Ohio is bounded by the Ohio River, but nearly all of the river itself belongs to Kentucky and West Virginia.

sentence: In 1980, the US Supreme Court held that, based on the wording of the cessation of territory by Virginia (which at the time included what is now Kentucky and West Virginia), the boundary between Ohio and Kentucky (and, by implication, West Virginia) is the northern low-water mark of the river as it existed in 1792.

name: ohio
sentence: The climate of Ohio is a humid continental climate (Köppen climate classification Dfa/Dfb) throughout most of the state, except in the extreme southern counties of Ohio's Bluegrass region section, which are located on the northern periphery of the humid subtropical climate (Cfa) and Upland South region of the United States.

sentence: Many major east–west transportation corridors go through Ohio.

sentence: The state government of Ohio consists of the executive, legislative, and judicial branches.

name: ohio
sentence: A lieutenant governor succeeds the governor in the event of any removal from office, and performs any duties assigned by the governor.

name: ohio
sentence: The other elected constitutional offices in the executive branch are the secretary of state (Frank LaRose), auditor (Keith Faber), treasurer (Robert Sprague), and attorney general (Dave Yost).

name: ohio
sentence: The Ohio General Assembly is a bicameral legislature consisting of the Senatorte and House of Representatives.

name: ohio
sentence: Each senator represents approximately 330,000 constituents.

name: ohio
sentence: The House of Representatives is composed of 99 members.

name: ohio
sentence: The Republican Party is the controlling party in both houses as of the 2020 election cycle.

name: ohio
sentence: In order to be enacted into law, a bill must be adopted by both houses of the General Assembly and signed by the Governor.

name: ohio
sentence: If the Governor vetoes a bill, the General Assembly can override the veto with a three-fifths supermajority of both houses.

name: ohio

name: ohio
sentence: The session laws are published in the official Law of Ohio.

name: ohio
sentence: There are three levels of the Ohio state judiciary.

name: ohio
sentence: The lowest level is the court of common pleas: each county maintains its own constitutionally mandated court of common pleas, which maintain jurisdiction over "all justiciable matters".

name: ohio
sentence: The intermediate-level court system is the district court system.

name: ohio
sentence: Twelve courts of appeals exist, each retaining jurisdiction over appeals from common pleas, municipal, and county courts in a set geographical area.

name: ohio
sentence: A case heard in this system is decided by a three-judge panel, and each judge is elected.The state's highest-ranking court is the Ohio Supreme Court.

name: ohio
sentence: A seven-justice panel composes the court, which, by its own discretion, hears appeals from the courts of appeals, and retains original jurisdiction over limited matters.

name: ohio
sentence: There are also several levels of local government in Ohio: counties, municipalities (cities and villages), townships, special districts and school districts.

name: ohio

sentence: Summit County and Cuyahoga County have chosen an alternate form of government.

name: ohio
sentence: The other counties have a government with a three-member board of county commissioners, a sheriff, coroner, auditor, treasurer, clerk of the court of common pleas prosecutor, engineer, and recorder.There are two kinds of incorporated municipalities, 251 cities and 681 villages.

name: ohio

name: ohio
sentence: Townships may have limited home rule powers.There are more than 600 city, local, and exempted village school districts providing K-12 education in Ohio, as well as about four dozen joint vocation school districts which are separate from the K-12 districts.

name: ohio
sentence: Six US presidents hailed from Ohio at the time of their elections, giving rise to its nickname "mother of presidents", a sobriquet it shares with Virginia.

sentence: It is also termed "modern mother of presidents", in contrast to Virginia's status as the origin of presidents earlier in American history.

name: ohio

sentence: All seven were Republicans.

sentence: Ohio is considered a swing state, being won by either the Democratic or Republican candidates reasonably each election.

sentence: As a swing state, Ohio is usually targeted by both major-party campaigns, especially in competitive elections.

sentence: South Dakota has several sites administered by the National Park Service.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Two national parks have been established in the state, both in its southwestern region.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Wind Cave National Park, established in 1903 in the Black Hills, has an extensive cave network and is home to a large herd of bison.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Badlands National Park was established in 1978, and features an eroded, brightly colored landscape surrounded by semi-arid grasslands.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Mount Rushmore National Memorial in the Black Hills was established in 1925.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The sculpture of four US Presidents was carved into the mountainside by sculptor Gutzon Borglum.Other areas managed by the National Park Service include Jewel Cave National Monument near Custer, the Lewis and Clark National Historic Trail, the Minuteman Missile National Historic Site, which features a decommissioned nuclear missile silo and a separate missile control area several miles away, and the Missouri National Recreational River.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The Crazy Horse Memorial is a large mountainside sculpture near Mount Rushmore being built using private funds.

name: south_dakota

sentence: At the 2022 estimate South Dakota's population was 909,824 on July 1, 2022, a 2.61% increase since the 2020 United States census.7.3% of South Dakota's population was reported as under 5, 24% under 18, and 14.3% were 65 or older.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Females made up approximately 50.2% of the population.

sentence: As of the 2000 census, South Dakota ranked fifth-lowest in the nation in population and population density, only North Dakota, Alaska, Vermont, and Wyoming have fewer residents.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Of the people residing in South Dakota, 65.7% were born in South Dakota, 31.4% were born in another US state, 0.6% were born in Puerto Rico, US Island areas, or born abroad to American parent(s), and 2.3% were born in another country.The center of population of South Dakota is in Buffalo County, in the unincorporated county seat of Gann Valley.According to HUD's 2022 Annual Homeless Assessment Report, there were an estimated 1,389 homeless people in South Dakota.

sentence: According to the 2010 census, the racial composition of the population was: 84.7% White (83.8% non-Hispanic white) 8.8% American Indian and Alaska Native 1.2% African American or black 0.9% Asian American 0.1% from some other race 1.8% of two or more racesEthnically, 2.7% of South Dakota's population was of Hispanic, Latino, or Spanish origin (they may be of any race).

sentence: As of 2011, 25.4% of South Dakota's population younger than age 1 were minorities, meaning they had at least one parent who was not non-Hispanic white.As of 2000, the five largest ancestry groups in South Dakota are German (40.7%), Norwegian (15.3%), Irish (10.4%), Native American (8.3%), and English (7.1%).German Americans are the largest ancestry group in most parts of the state, especially in East River (east of the Missouri River), although there are also large Scandinavian-descended populations in some counties.

name: south_dakota
sentence: South Dakota has the nation's largest population of Hutterites, a communal Anabaptist group which emigrated in 1874 from German-speaking villages in what today is Ukraine but at that time was part of the Russian Empire.

name: south_dakota
sentence: American Indians, largely Lakota, Dakota, and Nakota (Sioux), are predominant in several counties and constitute 20 percent of the population in West River.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The seven large Indian reservations in the state occupy an area much diminished from their former Great Sioux Reservation of West River, which the federal government had once allocated to the Sioux tribes.

sentence: South Dakota has the third-highest proportion of Native Americans of any state, behind Alaska and New Mexico.Five of the state's counties are wholly within the boundaries of sovereign Indian reservations.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Because of the limitations of climate and land, and isolation from urban areas with more employment opportunities, living standards on many South Dakota reservations are often far below the national average; Ziebach County ranked as the poorest county in the nation in 2009.

sentence: A 1995 study by the US Census Bureau found 58% of homes on the Pine Ridge Indian Reservation did not have a telephone.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The reservations' isolation also inhibits their ability to generate revenue from gaming casinos, an avenue that has proved profitable for many tribes closer to urban centers.

sentence: In 1995 the legislature passed a law to make English the "common language" of the state.

sentence: Since 2019, "the language of the Great Sioux Nation, comprised of three dialects, Dakota, Lakota, and Nakota" is the official indigenous language.

sentence: As of the 2000 census, 1.90% of the population age 5 or older speak German at home, while 1.51% speak Lakota or Dakota, and 1.43% Spanish.

name: south_dakota
sentence: As of 2010, 93.46% (692,504) of South Dakota residents age 5 and older spoke English as their primary language.

name: south_dakota
sentence: 6.54% of the population spoke a language other than English.

name: south_dakota
sentence: 2.06% (15,292) of the population spoke Spanish, 1.39% (10,282) spoke Dakota, and 1.37% (10,140) spoke German.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Other languages spoken included Vietnamese (0.16%), Chinese (0.12%), and Russian (0.10%).

name: south_dakota
sentence: Over the last several decades, the population in many rural areas has declined in South Dakota, in common with other Great Plains states.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The change has been characterized as "rural flight" as family farming has declined.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Young people have moved to cities for other employment.

name: south_dakota
sentence: This trend has continued in recent years, with 30 of South Dakota's counties losing population between the 1990 and the 2000 census.

name: south_dakota
sentence: During that time, nine counties had a population loss of greater than 10%, with Harding County, in the northwest corner of the state, losing nearly 19% of its population.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Low birth rates and a lack of younger immigration has caused the median age of many of these counties to increase.

name: south_dakota
sentence: In 24 counties, at least 20% of the population is over the age of 65, compared with a national rate of 12.8%.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The effect of rural flight has not been spread evenly through South Dakota, however.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Although most rural counties and small towns have lost population, the Sioux Falls area, the larger counties along Interstate 29, the Black Hills, and many Indian reservations have all gained population.

name: south_dakota
sentence: As the reservations have exercised more sovereignty, some Sioux have returned to them from urban areas.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Lincoln County near Sioux Falls was the seventh fastest-growing county (by percentage) in the United States in 2010.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The growth in these areas has compensated for losses in the rest of the state.

name: south_dakota
sentence: South Dakota's total population continues to increase steadily, albeit at a slower rate than the national average.

name: south_dakota
sentence: According to the Public Religion Research Institute in 2020, 73% of the adult population were Christian.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Per the Pew Research Center's separate 2014 study, the largest religious denominations in Christianity by number of adherents as a percentage of South Dakota's population in 2014 were the Catholic Church with 22 percent, evangelical Protestants with 25 percent, and mainline Protestants with 32 percent.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Together, all kinds of Protestants accounted for 57 percent.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Those unaffiliated with any religion represented 18 percent of the population.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The breakdown of other religions was <1% Muslim, <1% Hindu and 1% Buddhist.The largest Christian denominations by number of adherents in 2010 were the Roman Catholic Church with 148,883 members; the Evangelical Lutheran Church in America (ELCA) with 112,649 members; and the United Methodist Church (UMC) with 36,020 members.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The ELCA and UMC are specific denominations within the broader terms 'Lutheran' and 'Methodist', respectively.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Through the Association of Religion Data Archives in 2020, Catholicism remained the largest Christian denomination, followed by the ELCA.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Non-denominational Protestants numbered 63,992, becoming the third largest group of Christians throughout the state.In 2022, the Public Religion Research Institute determined 72% of the state were Christian altogether, though Protestants were 48%, Catholics 22%, and Jehovah's Witnesses 2%.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The religiously unaffiliated declined from 22% to 21% between 2020 and 2022.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Other non-Christian faith groups with a substantial presence in the South Dakota were Buddhism (3%), New Age (3%), and others at 1% altogether.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Through the Association of Religion Data Archives 2020 study, there were 978 adherents to the Baha'i Faith and 535 Muslims.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The current-dollar gross state product of South Dakota was $39.8 billion as of 2010, the fifth-smallest total state output in the US

name: south_dakota
sentence: The per capita personal income was $38,865 in 2010, ranked 25th in the US, and 12.5% of the population was below the poverty line in 2008.

name: south_dakota
sentence: CNBC's list of "Top States for Business for 2010" has recognized South Dakota as the seventh best state in the nation.

name: south_dakota
sentence: In July 2011, the state's unemployment rate was 4.7%.The service industry is the largest economic contributor in South Dakota.

name: south_dakota
sentence: This sector includes the retail, finance, and health care industries.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Citibank, which was at one time the largest bank holding company in the United States, established national banking operations in South Dakota in 1981 to take advantage of favorable banking regulations.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Government spending is another important segment of the state's economy, providing over ten percent of the gross state product.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Ellsworth Air Force Base, near Rapid City, is the second-largest single employer in the state.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Agriculture has historically been a key component of the South Dakota economy.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Although other industries have expanded rapidly in recent decades, agricultural production is still very important to the state's economy, especially in rural areas.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The five most valuable agricultural products in South Dakota are cattle, corn (maize), soybeans, wheat, and hogs.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Agriculture-related industries such as meat packing and ethanol production also have a considerable economic impact on the state.

name: south_dakota
sentence: South Dakota is the sixth leading ethanol-producing state in the nation.Another important sector in South Dakota's economy is tourism.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Many travel to view the attractions of the state, particularly those in the Black Hills region, such as historic Deadwood, Mount Rushmore, and the nearby state and national parks.

name: south_dakota
sentence: One of the largest tourist events in the state is the annual Sturgis Motorcycle Rally.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The five-day event drew over 739,000 attendees in 2015; significant considering the state has a total population of 850,000.

name: south_dakota
sentence: In 2006, tourism provided an estimated 33,000 jobs in the state and contributed over two billion dollars to the economy of South Dakota.

name: south_dakota
sentence: South Dakota has 83,609 miles (134,556 km) of highways, roads, and streets, along with 679 miles (1,093 km) of interstate highways.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Two major interstates pass through South Dakota: Interstate 90, which runs east and west through the southern half of the state; and Interstate 29, running north and south in the eastern portion of the state.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The I-29 corridor features generally higher rates of population and economic growth than areas in eastern South Dakota further from the interstate.Also in the state are the shorter Interstates 190, a spur into central Rapid City, and 229, a loop around southern and eastern Sioux Falls.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Several major US highways pass through the state.

name: south_dakota
sentence: US routes 12, 14, 16, 18 and 212 travel east and west, while US routes 81, 83, 85 and 281 run north and south.

name: south_dakota
sentence: South Dakota and Montana are the only states sharing a land border that is not traversed by a paved road.

name: south_dakota
sentence: South Dakota contains two National Scenic Byways.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The Peter Norbeck National Scenic Byway is in the Black Hills, while the Native American Scenic Byway runs along the Missouri River in the north-central part of the state.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Other scenic byways include the Badlands Loop Scenic Byway, the Spearfish Canyon Scenic Byway, and the Wildlife Loop Road Scenic Byway.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Railroads have played an important role in South Dakota transportation since the mid-19th century.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Some 4,420 miles (7,110 km) of railroad track were built in South Dakota during the late 19th century and early 20th century, but only 1,839 miles (2,960 km) are active.

name: south_dakota
sentence: BNSF Railway is the largest railroad in South Dakota; the Rapid City, Pierre and Eastern Railroad (formerly the Dakota, Minnesota and Eastern) is the state's other major carrier.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Other state carriers include Dakota Southern Railway, Dakota and Iowa Railroad, Ellis and Eastern Railroad, Sunflour Railroad, Canadian Pacific Railway, and the Sisseton Milbank Railroad.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Rail transportation in the state is mostly freight, but there are two passenger heritage railroads: the Black Hills Central and the Prairie Village, Herman, and Milwaukee.

name: south_dakota
sentence: However, South Dakota is one of the two contiguous states that lack Amtrak service.

name: south_dakota
sentence: (South Dakota is the only contiguous state that never had Amtrak—Wyoming used to be served by the San Francisco Zephyr and the Pioneer.

name: south_dakota
sentence: )South Dakota's largest commercial airports in terms of passenger traffic are the Sioux Falls Regional Airport and Rapid City Regional Airport.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Delta Air Lines, Frontier Airlines, and Allegiant Airlines, as well as commuter airlines using the brand affiliation with major airlines serve the two largest airports.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Several other cities in the state also have commercial air service: Aberdeen Regional Airport, Pierre Regional Airport, and Watertown Regional Airport, some of which are subsidized by the Essential Air Service program.Public transit played a large role in the development of cities in South Dakota.

name: south_dakota
sentence: There were seven cities with a streetcar system in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, however, all of these were discontinued over time.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Today, only three fixed route public transit systems exist in the state, those being in Sioux Falls, Rapid City and on the Yankton Reservation.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Like other US states, the structure of the government of South Dakota follows the same separation of powers as the federal government, with executive, legislative, and judicial branches.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The structure of the state government is laid out in the Constitution of South Dakota, the highest law in the state.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The constitution may be amended by a majority vote of both houses of the legislature, or by voter initiative.The Governor of South Dakota occupies the executive branch of the state government.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The current governor is Kristi Noem, a Republican.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The state constitution gives the governor the power to sign into law or veto bills passed by the state legislature, to serve as commander-in-chief of the South Dakota National Guard, to appoint a cabinet, and to commute criminal sentences or to pardon those convicted of crimes.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The governor serves for a four-year term, and may not serve more than two consecutive terms.The state legislature is made up of two bodies, the Senatorte, which has 35 members, and the House of Representatives, with 70 members.

name: south_dakota
sentence: South Dakota is divided into 35 legislative districts, with voters electing two representatives and one senator per district.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The legislature meets for an annual session which begins on the second Tuesday in January and lasts for 30 days; it also meets if a special session is called by the governor.The judicial branch is made up of several levels.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The state supreme court, with four justices and a chief justice, is the highest court in the state.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Below the supreme court are the circuit courts; 41 circuit judges serve in seven judicial circuits in the state.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Below the circuit courts are the magistrate courts, which deal with lesser criminal and civil actions.

name: south_dakota
sentence: As of 2005, South Dakota has the lowest per capita total state tax rate in the United States.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The state does not levy personal or corporate income taxes, inheritance taxes, or taxes on intangible personal property.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The state sales tax rate is 4.5 percent.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Various localities have local levies so in some areas the rate is six percent.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The state sales tax does not apply to sales to Indians on Indian reservations, but many reservations have a compact with the state.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Businesses on the reservation collect the tax and the state refunds to the Indian Tribes the percentage of sales tax collections relating to the ratio of Indian population to total population in the county or area affected.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Ad valorem property taxes are local taxes and are a large source of funding for school systems, counties, municipalities and other local government units.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The South Dakota Special Tax Division regulates some taxes including cigarette and alcohol-related taxes.

name: south_dakota
sentence: South Dakota is represented at the federal level by Senatortor John Thune, Senatortor Mike Rounds, and Representative Dusty Johnson.

name: south_dakota
sentence: All three are Republicans.

name: south_dakota
sentence: South Dakota is one of seven states with only one seat in the US House of Representatives.

name: south_dakota
sentence: In United States presidential elections, South Dakota is allotted three of 538 votes in the Electoral College.

name: south_dakota
sentence: As in all other states except Maine and neighboring Nebraska, South Dakota's electoral votes are granted in a winner-take-all system.

name: south_dakota
sentence: South Dakota politics are generally dominated by the Republican Party.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Since statehood, Republicans have carried the state's electoral votes in all but five presidential elections: 1896, 1912 (by Theodore Roosevelt's Progressive Party), 1932, 1936 and 1964.

name: south_dakota
sentence: (Democrat George McGovern—a native South Dakotan—failed to carry his home state in 1972.)

name: south_dakota
sentence: Only Alaska has been carried fewer times by a Democrat.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Additionally, a Democrat has not won the governorship since 1974.

name: south_dakota
sentence: As of 2016, Republicans hold a 15% voter registration advantage over Democrats and hold supermajorities in both the state House and the state Senatorte.Despite the state's general Republican and conservative leanings, Democrats have found success in various statewide elections, most notably in those involving South Dakota's congressional representatives in Washington.

name: south_dakota
sentence: American Indians have been becoming more active in state and county electoral politics.

name: south_dakota
sentence: In the 2002 election, American Indian voting carried Tim Johnson as the Democratic candidate by a margin of 532 votes.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Until his electoral defeat in 2004, Senatortor Tom Daschle was the Senatorte minority leader (and briefly its majority leader during Democratic control of the Senatorte in 2001–02).

name: south_dakota
sentence: Other prominent South Dakota Democrats include former presidential nominees George McGovern and Hubert Humphrey.

name: south_dakota
sentence: In 2016, South Dakota voted for Republican nominee Donald Trump over Democratic nominee Hillary Clinton by a margin of 30%.

name: south_dakota
sentence: In 2018, Republican congresswoman Kristi Noem defeated Democrat Billie Sutton in the gubernatorial election by a small margin, and Republican Dusty Johnson defeated Democrat Tim Bjorkman for the state's at-large seat in the US House of Representatives.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Noem was sworn in on January 5, 2019, making her the first female governor of the state.Contemporary political issues in South Dakota include the costs and benefits of the state lottery, South Dakota's relatively low rankings in education spending (particularly teacher pay—recently the State Sales Tax was increased from 4% to 4.5% to finance an increase in teacher pay), and recent legislative and electoral attempts to ban abortion in the state.A Republican-supported bill passed in March 2019 requires that all public schools display "In God We Trust" in a prominent location.In a 2020 study, South Dakota was ranked as the 22nd hardest state for citizens to vote in.

name: south_dakota
sentence: South Dakota's culture reflects the state's American Indian, rural, Western, and European roots.

name: south_dakota
sentence: A number of annual events celebrating the state's ethnic and historical heritage take place around the state, such as Days of '76 in Deadwood, Czech Days in Tabor, and the annual St. Patrick's Day and Cinco de Mayo festivities in Sioux Falls.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The various tribes hold many annual pow wows at their reservations throughout the state, to which non-Native Americans are sometimes invited.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Custer State Park holds an annual Buffalo Roundup, in which volunteers on horseback gather the park's herd of around 1,500 bison.Black Elk (Lakota) was a medicine man and heyokha, whose life spanned the transition to reservations.

name: south_dakota
sentence: His accounts of the 19th-century Indian Wars and Ghost Dance movement, and his deep thoughts on personal visions and Native American religion, form the basis of the book Black Elk Speaks, first published in 1932.

sentence: (Among several editions, a premier annotated edition was published in 2008.)

sentence: Paul Goble, an award-winning children's book author and illustrator, was based in the Black Hills from 1977.Laura Ingalls Wilder, whose semi-autobiographical books are based on her experiences as a child and young adult on the frontier, is one of South Dakota's best-known writers.

name: south_dakota
sentence: She drew from her life growing up on a homestead near De Smet as the basis for five of her novels: By the Shores of Silver Lake, The Long Winter, Little Town on the Prairie, These Happy Golden Years, and The First Four Years.

sentence: These gained renewed popularity in the United States when Little House on the Prairie was adapted and produced as a television series in 1974.

sentence: Wilder's daughter, Rose Wilder Lane, who became a well-known writer in her own right, was born near De Smet in 1886.

sentence: South Dakota has also produced several notable artists.

sentence: Harvey Dunn grew up on a homestead near Manchester in the late 19th century.

sentence: While Dunn worked most of his career as a commercial illustrator, his most famous works showed various scenes of frontier life; he completed these near the end of his career.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Oscar Howe (Crow) was born on the Crow Creek Indian Reservation and won fame for his watercolor paintings.

sentence: Howe was one of the first Native American painters to adopt techniques and style heavily influenced by the mid-20th century abstraction movement, rather than relying on traditional Native American styles.

sentence: Many of his works are on display at the Redlin Art Center in Watertown.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Sioux Falls is the largest city in South Dakota, with a 2020 population of 192,517, and a metropolitan area population of 281,958.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The city, founded in 1856, is in the southeast corner of the state.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Retail, finance, and healthcare have assumed greater importance in Sioux Falls, where the economy was originally centered on agri-business and quarrying.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Rapid City, with a 2020 population of 74,703, and a metropolitan area population of 144,558, is the second-largest city in the state.

name: south_dakota
sentence: It is on the eastern edge of the Black Hills, and was founded in 1876.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Rapid City's economy is largely based on tourism and defense spending, because of the proximity of many tourist attractions in the Black Hills and Ellsworth Air Force Base.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The next eight largest cities in the state, in order of descending 2010 population, are Aberdeen (28,495), Brookings (23,337), Watertown (22,655), Mitchell (15,660), Yankton (15,411), Huron (14,263), Pierre (14,091), and Spearfish (12,193).

name: south_dakota
sentence: Pierre is the state capital, and Brookings and Vermillion are the locations of the state's two largest universities (South Dakota State University and University of South Dakota, respectively).

name: south_dakota
sentence: With a population of about 14,000, Pierre is the second smallest state capital in the United States.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Of the ten largest cities in the state, only Rapid City and Spearfish are west of the Missouri River.

name: south_dakota
sentence: South Dakota's first newspaper, the Dakota Democrat, began publishing in Yankton in 1858.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Today, the state's largest newspaper is the Sioux Falls Argus Leader, with a Sunday circulation of 63,701 and a weekday circulation of 44,334.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The Rapid City Journal, with a Sunday circulation of 32,638 and a weekday circulation of 27,827, is South Dakota's second largest newspaper.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The next four largest newspapers in the state are the Aberdeen American News, the Watertown Public Opinion, the Huron Plainsman, and the Brookings Register.

name: south_dakota
sentence: In 1981, Tim Giago founded the Lakota Times as a newspaper for the local American Indian community on the Pine Ridge Indian Reservation.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The newspaper, now published in New York and known as Indian Country Today, is available in every state in the country.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The Sioux City Journal also covers parts of South Dakota.

name: south_dakota
sentence: There are nine television stations broadcasting in South Dakota; South Dakota Public Television broadcasts from a number of locations around the state, while the other stations broadcast from Sioux Falls or Rapid City.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The two largest television media markets in South Dakota are Sioux Falls-Mitchell, with a viewership of 246,020, and Rapid City, with a viewership of 91,070.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The two markets rank as 114th and 177th largest in the United States, respectively.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The state's first television station, KELO-TV, began airing in Sioux Falls in 1953.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Among KELO's early programs was Captain 11, an afternoon children's program.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Captain 11 ran from 1955 until 1996, making it the nation's longest continuously running children's television program.A number of South Dakotans are famous for their work in television and publishing.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Former NBC Nightly News anchor and author Tom Brokaw is from Webster and Yankton, USA Today founder Al Neuharth was from Eureka and Alpena, gameshow host Bob Barker spent much of his childhood in Mission, and entertainment news hosts Pat O'Brien and Mary Hart are from Sioux Falls.

name: south_dakota
sentence: As of 2006, South Dakota has a total primary and secondary school enrollment of 136,872, with 120,278 of these students being educated in the public school system.

name: south_dakota
sentence: There are 703 public schools in 168 school districts, giving South Dakota the highest number of schools per capita in the United States.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The current high school graduation rate is 89.9%, and the average ACT score is 21.8, slightly above the national average of 21.1.

name: south_dakota
sentence: 89.8% of the adult population has earned at least a high school diploma, and 25.8% has earned a bachelor's degree or higher.

name: south_dakota
sentence: South Dakota's 2008 average public school teacher salary of $36,674 was the lowest in the nation (national average was $52,308).

name: south_dakota
sentence: In 2007 South Dakota passed legislation modeled after Montana's Indian Education for All Act (1999), mandating education about Native American tribal history, culture, and heritage in all the schools, from pre-school through college, in an effort to increase knowledge and appreciation about Indian culture among all residents of the state, as well as to reinforce Indian students' understanding of their own cultures' contributions.The South Dakota Board of Regents, whose members are appointed by the governor, controls the six public universities in the state.

name: south_dakota
sentence: South Dakota State University (SDSU), in Brookings, is the state's largest university, with an enrollment of 12,831.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The University of South Dakota (USD), in Vermillion, is the state's oldest university, and has South Dakota's only law school and medical school.

name: south_dakota
sentence: South Dakota also has several private universities, the largest of which is Augustana University in Sioux Falls.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Because of its low population, South Dakota does not host any major league professional sports franchises.

name: south_dakota
sentence: The state has minor league and independent league teams, all of which play in Sioux Falls or Rapid City.

name: south_dakota
sentence: Sioux Falls is home to four teams: the Sioux Falls Canaries (baseball), the Sioux Falls Skyforce (basketball), the Sioux Falls Stampede (hockey), and the Sioux Falls Storm (indoor American football).

name: south_dakota
